Psalms 22:9.title: Psalms 22:9-10
Psalms 22:9.content: Though ironically spoken, the exhortation to trust was well founded on his previous experience of divine aid, the special illustration of which is drawn from the period of helpless infancy. didst make me hope—literally, "made me secure."

Psalms 22:10.title: Psalms 22:9-10
Psalms 22:10.content: Though ironically spoken, the exhortation to trust was well founded on his previous experience of divine aid, the special illustration of which is drawn from the period of helpless infancy. didst make me hope—literally, "made me secure."

Psalms 22:11.title: Psalms 22:11
Psalms 22:11.content: From this statement of reasons for the appeal, he renews it, pleading his double extremity, the nearness of trouble, and the absence of a helper.

Psalms 22:12.title: Psalms 22:12-13
Psalms 22:12.content: His enemies, with the vigor of bulls and rapacity of lions, surround him, eagerly seeking his ruin. The force of both figures is greater without the use of any particle denoting comparison.

Psalms 22:13.title: Psalms 22:12-13
Psalms 22:13.content: His enemies, with the vigor of bulls and rapacity of lions, surround him, eagerly seeking his ruin. The force of both figures is greater without the use of any particle denoting comparison.

Psalms 22:14.title: Psalms 22:14-15
Psalms 22:14.content: Utter exhaustion and hopeless weakness, in these circumstances of pressing danger, are set forth by the most expressive figures; the solidity of the body is destroyed, and it becomes like water; the bones are parted; the heart, the very seat of vitality, melts like wax; all the juices of the system are dried up; the tongue can no longer perform its office, but lies parched and stiffened (compare Ge 49:4; 2Sa 14:14; Ps 58:8). In this, God is regarded as the ultimate source, and men as the instruments.

Psalms 22:15.title: Psalms 22:14-15
Psalms 22:15.content: Utter exhaustion and hopeless weakness, in these circumstances of pressing danger, are set forth by the most expressive figures; the solidity of the body is destroyed, and it becomes like water; the bones are parted; the heart, the very seat of vitality, melts like wax; all the juices of the system are dried up; the tongue can no longer perform its office, but lies parched and stiffened (compare Ge 49:4; 2Sa 14:14; Ps 58:8). In this, God is regarded as the ultimate source, and men as the instruments.

Psalms 22:15.title: Psalms 22:15
Psalms 22:15.content: the dust of death—of course, denotes the grave. We need not try to find the exact counterpart of each item of the description in the particulars of our Saviour's sufferings. Figurative language resembles pictures of historical scenes, presenting substantial truth, under illustrations, which, though not essential to the facts, are not inconsistent with them. Were any portion of Christ's terrible sufferings specially designed, it was doubtless that of the garden of Gethsemane.

Psalms 22:16.title: Psalms 22:16
Psalms 22:16.content: Evildoers are well described as dogs, which, in the East, herding together, wild and rapacious, are justly objects of great abhorrence. The last clause has been a subject of much discussion (involving questions as to the genuineness of the Hebrew word translated "pierce)" which cannot be made intelligible to the English reader. Though not quoted in the New Testament, the remarkable aptness of the description to the facts of the Saviour's history, together with difficulties attending any other mode of explaining the clause in the Hebrew, justify an adherence to the terms of our version and their obvious meaning.

Psalms 22:17.title: Psalms 22:17
Psalms 22:17.content: His emaciated frame, itself an item of his misery, is rendered more so as the object of delighted contemplation to his enemies. The verbs, "look" and "stare," often occur as suggestive of feelings of satisfaction (compare Ps 27:13; 54:7; 118:7).

Psalms 22:18.title: Psalms 22:18
Psalms 22:18.content: This literally fulfilled prediction closes the sad picture of the exposed and deserted sufferer.

Psalms 22:19.title: Psalms 22:19-20
Psalms 22:19.content: He now turns with unabated desire and trust to God, who, in His strength and faithfulness, is contrasted with the urgent dangers described.

Psalms 22:20.title: Psalms 22:19-20
Psalms 22:20.content: He now turns with unabated desire and trust to God, who, in His strength and faithfulness, is contrasted with the urgent dangers described.

Psalms 22:20.title: Psalms 22:20
Psalms 22:20.content: my soul—or self (compare Ps 3:2; 16:10). my darling—literally, "my only one," or, "solitary one," as desolate and afflicted (Ps 25:16; 35:17).

Psalms 22:21.title: Psalms 22:21
Psalms 22:21.content: Deliverance pleaded in view of former help, when in the most imminent danger, from the most powerful enemy, represented by the unicorn or wild buffalo. the lion's mouth—(Compare Ps 22:13). The lion often used as a figure representing violent enemies; the connecting of the mouth intimates their rapacity.

Psalms 22:22.title: Psalms 22:22-24
Psalms 22:22.content: He declares his purpose to celebrate God's gracious dealings and publish His manifested perfections ("name," Ps 5:11), &c., and forthwith he invites the pious (those who have a reverential fear of God) to unite in special praise for a deliverance, illustrating God's kind regard for the lowly, whom men neglect [Ps 22:24]. To hide the face (or eyes) expresses a studied neglect of one's cause, and refusal of aid or sympathy (compare Ps 30:7; Isa 1:15).

Psalms 22:23.title: Psalms 22:22-24
Psalms 22:23.content: He declares his purpose to celebrate God's gracious dealings and publish His manifested perfections ("name," Ps 5:11), &c., and forthwith he invites the pious (those who have a reverential fear of God) to unite in special praise for a deliverance, illustrating God's kind regard for the lowly, whom men neglect [Ps 22:24]. To hide the face (or eyes) expresses a studied neglect of one's cause, and refusal of aid or sympathy (compare Ps 30:7; Isa 1:15).

Psalms 22:24.title: Psalms 22:22-24
Psalms 22:24.content: He declares his purpose to celebrate God's gracious dealings and publish His manifested perfections ("name," Ps 5:11), &c., and forthwith he invites the pious (those who have a reverential fear of God) to unite in special praise for a deliverance, illustrating God's kind regard for the lowly, whom men neglect [Ps 22:24]. To hide the face (or eyes) expresses a studied neglect of one's cause, and refusal of aid or sympathy (compare Ps 30:7; Isa 1:15).

Psalms 22:25.title: Psalms 22:25-26
Psalms 22:25.content: My praise shall be of thee—or, perhaps better, "from thee," that is, God gives grace to praise Him. With offering praise, he further evinces his gratitude by promising the payment of his vows, in celebrating the usual festival, as provided in the law (De 12:18; 16:11), of which the pious or humble, and they that seek the Lord (His true worshippers) shall partake abundantly, and join him in praise [Ps 22:26]. In the enthusiasm produced by his lively feelings, he addresses such in words, assuring them of God's perpetual favor [Ps 22:26]. The dying of the heart denotes death (1Sa 25:37); so its living denotes life.

Psalms 22:26.title: Psalms 22:25-26
Psalms 22:26.content: My praise shall be of thee—or, perhaps better, "from thee," that is, God gives grace to praise Him. With offering praise, he further evinces his gratitude by promising the payment of his vows, in celebrating the usual festival, as provided in the law (De 12:18; 16:11), of which the pious or humble, and they that seek the Lord (His true worshippers) shall partake abundantly, and join him in praise [Ps 22:26]. In the enthusiasm produced by his lively feelings, he addresses such in words, assuring them of God's perpetual favor [Ps 22:26]. The dying of the heart denotes death (1Sa 25:37); so its living denotes life.

Psalms 22:27.title: Psalms 22:27-31
Psalms 22:27.content: His case illustrates God's righteous government. Beyond the existing time and people, others shall be brought to acknowledge and worship God; the fat ones, or the rich as well as the poor, the helpless who cannot keep themselves alive, shall together unite in celebrating God's delivering power, and transmit to unborn people the records of His grace.

Psalms 22:28.title: Psalms 22:27-31
Psalms 22:28.content: His case illustrates God's righteous government. Beyond the existing time and people, others shall be brought to acknowledge and worship God; the fat ones, or the rich as well as the poor, the helpless who cannot keep themselves alive, shall together unite in celebrating God's delivering power, and transmit to unborn people the records of His grace.

Psalms 22:29.title: Psalms 22:27-31
Psalms 22:29.content: His case illustrates God's righteous government. Beyond the existing time and people, others shall be brought to acknowledge and worship God; the fat ones, or the rich as well as the poor, the helpless who cannot keep themselves alive, shall together unite in celebrating God's delivering power, and transmit to unborn people the records of His grace.

Psalms 22:30.title: Psalms 22:27-31
Psalms 22:30.content: His case illustrates God's righteous government. Beyond the existing time and people, others shall be brought to acknowledge and worship God; the fat ones, or the rich as well as the poor, the helpless who cannot keep themselves alive, shall together unite in celebrating God's delivering power, and transmit to unborn people the records of His grace.

Psalms 22:30.title: Psalms 22:30
Psalms 22:30.content: it shall be accounted to the Lord for, &c.—or, "it shall be told of the Lord to a generation." God's wonderful works shall be told from generation to generation.

Psalms 22:31.title: Psalms 22:27-31
Psalms 22:31.content: His case illustrates God's righteous government. Beyond the existing time and people, others shall be brought to acknowledge and worship God; the fat ones, or the rich as well as the poor, the helpless who cannot keep themselves alive, shall together unite in celebrating God's delivering power, and transmit to unborn people the records of His grace.

Psalms 22:31.title: Psalms 22:31
Psalms 22:31.content: that he hath done this—supply "it," or "this"—that is, what the Psalm has unfolded.

Psalms 23:1.title: Psalms 23:1
Psalms 23:1.content: Christ's relation to His people is often represented by the figure of a shepherd (Joh 10:14; Heb 13:20; 1Pe 2:25; 5:4), and therefore the opinion that He is the Lord here so described, and in Ge 48:15; Ps 80:1; Isa 40:11, is not without some good reason.

Psalms 23:2.title: Psalms 23:2
Psalms 23:2.content: green pastures—or, "pastures of tender grass," are mentioned, not in respect to food, but as places of cool and refreshing rest. the still waters—are, literally, "waters of "stillness," whose quiet flow invites to repose. They are contrasted with boisterous streams on the one hand, and stagnant, offensive pools on the other.

Psalms 23:3.title: Psalms 23:3
Psalms 23:3.content: To restore the soul is to revive or quicken it (Ps 19:7), or relieve it (La 1:11, 19). paths of righteousness—those of safety, as directed by God, and pleasing to Him. for his name's sake—or, regard for His perfections, pledged for His people's welfare.

Psalms 23:4.title: Psalms 23:4
Psalms 23:4.content: In the darkest and most trying hour God is near. the valley of the shadow of death—is a ravine overhung by high precipitous cliffs, filled with dense forests, and well calculated to inspire dread to the timid, and afford a covert to beasts of prey. While expressive of any great danger or cause of terror, it does not exclude the greatest of all, to which it is most popularly applied, and which its terms suggest. thy rod and thy staff—are symbols of a shepherd's office. By them he guides his sheep.

Psalms 23:5.title: Psalms 23:5-6
Psalms 23:5.content: Another figure expresses God's provided care. a table—or, "food," anointing oil—the symbol of gladness, and the overflowing cup—which represents abundance—are prepared for the child of God, who may feast in spite of his enemies, confident that this favor will ever attend him. This beautiful Psalm most admirably sets before us, in its chief figure, that of a shepherd, the gentle, kind, and sure care extended to God's people, who, as a shepherd, both rules and feeds them. The closing verse shows that the blessings mentioned are spiritual.

Psalms 23:6.title: Psalms 23:5-6
Psalms 23:6.content: Another figure expresses God's provided care. a table—or, "food," anointing oil—the symbol of gladness, and the overflowing cup—which represents abundance—are prepared for the child of God, who may feast in spite of his enemies, confident that this favor will ever attend him. This beautiful Psalm most admirably sets before us, in its chief figure, that of a shepherd, the gentle, kind, and sure care extended to God's people, who, as a shepherd, both rules and feeds them. The closing verse shows that the blessings mentioned are spiritual.

Psalms 24:1.title: Psalms 24:1
Psalms 24:1.content: fulness—everything. world—the habitable globe, with they that dwell—forming a parallel expression to the first clause.

Psalms 24:2.title: Psalms 24:2
Psalms 24:2.content: Poetically represents the facts of Ge 1:9.

Psalms 24:3.title: Psalms 24:3-4
Psalms 24:3.content: The form of a question gives vivacity. Hands, tongue, and heart are organs of action, speech, and feeling, which compose character. hill of the Lord—(compare Ps 2:6, &c.). His Church—the true or invisible, as typified by the earthly sanctuary.

Psalms 24:4.title: Psalms 24:3-4
Psalms 24:4.content: The form of a question gives vivacity. Hands, tongue, and heart are organs of action, speech, and feeling, which compose character. hill of the Lord—(compare Ps 2:6, &c.). His Church—the true or invisible, as typified by the earthly sanctuary.

Psalms 24:4.title: Psalms 24:4
Psalms 24:4.content: lifted up his soul—is to set the affections (Ps 25:1) on an object; here, vanity—or, any false thing, of which swearing falsely, or to falsehood, is a specification.

Psalms 24:5.title: Psalms 24:5
Psalms 24:5.content: righteousness—the rewards which God bestows on His people, or the grace to secure those rewards as well as the result.

Psalms 24:6.title: Psalms 24:6
Psalms 24:6.content: Jacob—By "Jacob," we may understand God's people (compare Isa 43:22; 44:2, &c.), corresponding to "the generation," as if he had said, "those who seek Thy face are Thy chosen people."

Psalms 24:7.title: Psalms 24:7-10
Psalms 24:7.content: The entrance of the ark, with the attending procession, into the holy sanctuary is pictured to us. The repetition of the terms gives emphasis.

Psalms 24:8.title: Psalms 24:7-10
Psalms 24:8.content: The entrance of the ark, with the attending procession, into the holy sanctuary is pictured to us. The repetition of the terms gives emphasis.

Psalms 24:9.title: Psalms 24:7-10
Psalms 24:9.content: The entrance of the ark, with the attending procession, into the holy sanctuary is pictured to us. The repetition of the terms gives emphasis.

Psalms 24:10.title: Psalms 24:7-10
Psalms 24:10.content: The entrance of the ark, with the attending procession, into the holy sanctuary is pictured to us. The repetition of the terms gives emphasis.

Psalms 24:10.title: Psalms 24:10
Psalms 24:10.content: Lord of hosts—or fully, Lord God of hosts (Ho 12:5; Am 4:13), describes God by a title indicative of supremacy over all creatures, and especially the heavenly armies (Jos 5:14; 1Ki 22:19). Whether, as some think, the actual enlargement of the ancient gates of Jerusalem be the basis of the figure, the effect of the whole is to impress us with a conception of the matchless majesty of God.

Psalms 25:1.title: Psalms 25:1
Psalms 25:1.content: lift up my soul—(Ps 24:4; 86:4), set my affections (compare Col 3:2).

Psalms 25:2.title: Psalms 25:2
Psalms 25:2.content: not be ashamed—by disappointment of hopes of relief.

Psalms 25:3.title: Psalms 25:3
Psalms 25:3.content: The prayer generalized as to all who wait on God—that is, who expect His favor. On the other hand, the disappointment of the perfidious, who, unprovoked, have done evil, is invoked (compare 2Sa 22:9).

Psalms 25:4.title: Psalms 25:4-5
Psalms 25:4.content: On the ground of former favor, he invokes divine guidance, according to God's gracious ways of dealing and faithfulness.

Psalms 25:5.title: Psalms 25:4-5
Psalms 25:5.content: On the ground of former favor, he invokes divine guidance, according to God's gracious ways of dealing and faithfulness.

Psalms 25:6.title: Psalms 25:6-7
Psalms 25:6.content: Confessing past and present sins, he pleads for mercy, not on palliations of sin, but on God's well-known benevolence.

Psalms 25:7.title: Psalms 25:6-7
Psalms 25:7.content: Confessing past and present sins, he pleads for mercy, not on palliations of sin, but on God's well-known benevolence.

Psalms 25:8.title: Psalms 25:8-9
Psalms 25:8.content: upright—acting according to His promise. sinners—the general term, limited by the meek—who are penitent. the way—and his way—God's way of providence.

Psalms 25:9.title: Psalms 25:8-9
Psalms 25:9.content: upright—acting according to His promise. sinners—the general term, limited by the meek—who are penitent. the way—and his way—God's way of providence.

Psalms 25:10.title: Psalms 25:10
Psalms 25:10.content: paths—similar sense—His modes of dealing (compare Ps 25:4). mercy and truth—(Job 14:1-22), God's grace in promising and faithfulness in performing.

Psalms 25:11.title: Psalms 25:11
Psalms 25:11.content: God's perfections of love, mercy, goodness, and truth are manifested (his name, compare Ps 9:10) in pardoning sin, and the greatness of sin renders pardon more needed.

Psalms 25:12.title: Psalms 25:12-13
Psalms 25:12.content: What he asks for himself is the common lot of all the pious.

Psalms 25:13.title: Psalms 25:12-13
Psalms 25:13.content: What he asks for himself is the common lot of all the pious.

Psalms 25:13.title: Psalms 25:13
Psalms 25:13.content: inherit the earth—(compare Mt 5:5). The phrase, alluding to the promise of Canaan, expresses all the blessings included in that promise, temporal as well as spiritual.

Psalms 25:14.title: Psalms 25:14
Psalms 25:14.content: The reason of the blessing explained—the pious enjoy communion with God (compare Pr 3:21, 12), and, of course, learn His gracious terms of pardon.

Psalms 25:15.title: Psalms 25:15
Psalms 25:15.content: His trust in God is fixed. net—is frequently used as a figure for dangers by enemies (Ps 9:15; 10:9).

Psalms 25:16.title: Psalms 25:16-19
Psalms 25:16.content: A series of earnest appeals for aid because God had seemed to desert him (compare Ps 13:1; 17:13, &c.), his sins oppressed him, his enemies had enlarged his troubles and were multiplied, increasing in hate and violence (Ps 9:8; 18:48).

Psalms 25:17.title: Psalms 25:16-19
Psalms 25:17.content: A series of earnest appeals for aid because God had seemed to desert him (compare Ps 13:1; 17:13, &c.), his sins oppressed him, his enemies had enlarged his troubles and were multiplied, increasing in hate and violence (Ps 9:8; 18:48).

Psalms 25:18.title: Psalms 25:16-19
Psalms 25:18.content: A series of earnest appeals for aid because God had seemed to desert him (compare Ps 13:1; 17:13, &c.), his sins oppressed him, his enemies had enlarged his troubles and were multiplied, increasing in hate and violence (Ps 9:8; 18:48).

Psalms 25:19.title: Psalms 25:16-19
Psalms 25:19.content: A series of earnest appeals for aid because God had seemed to desert him (compare Ps 13:1; 17:13, &c.), his sins oppressed him, his enemies had enlarged his troubles and were multiplied, increasing in hate and violence (Ps 9:8; 18:48).

Psalms 25:20.title: Psalms 25:20
Psalms 25:20.content: keep my soul—(Ps 16:1). put my trust—flee for refuge (Ps 2:12).

Psalms 25:21.title: Psalms 25:21
Psalms 25:21.content: In conscious innocence of the faults charged by his enemies, he confidently commits his cause to God. Some refer— integrity, &c.—to God, meaning His covenant faithfulness. This sense, though good, is an unusual application of the terms.

Psalms 25:22.title: Psalms 25:22
Psalms 25:22.content: Extend these blessings to all Thy people in all their distresses.

Psalms 26:1.title: Psalms 26:1
Psalms 26:1.content: Judge—decide on my case; the appeal of innocence. in mine integrity—freedom from blemish (compare Ps 25:21). His confidence of perseverance results from trust in God's sustaining grace.

Psalms 26:2.title: Psalms 26:2
Psalms 26:2.content: He asks the most careful scrutiny of his affections and thoughts (Ps 7:9), or motives.

Psalms 26:3.title: Psalms 26:3
Psalms 26:3.content: As often, the ground of prayer for present help is former favor.

Psalms 26:4.title: Psalms 26:4-8
Psalms 26:4.content: As exemplified by the fruits of divine grace, presented in his life, especially in his avoiding the wicked and his purposes of cleaving to God's worship.

Psalms 26:5.title: Psalms 26:4-8
Psalms 26:5.content: As exemplified by the fruits of divine grace, presented in his life, especially in his avoiding the wicked and his purposes of cleaving to God's worship.

Psalms 26:6.title: Psalms 26:4-8
Psalms 26:6.content: As exemplified by the fruits of divine grace, presented in his life, especially in his avoiding the wicked and his purposes of cleaving to God's worship.

Psalms 26:6.title: Psalms 26:6
Psalms 26:6.content: wash mine hands—expressive symbol of freedom from sinful acts (compare Mt 27:24).

Psalms 26:7.title: Psalms 26:4-8
Psalms 26:7.content: As exemplified by the fruits of divine grace, presented in his life, especially in his avoiding the wicked and his purposes of cleaving to God's worship.

Psalms 26:8.title: Psalms 26:4-8
Psalms 26:8.content: As exemplified by the fruits of divine grace, presented in his life, especially in his avoiding the wicked and his purposes of cleaving to God's worship.

Psalms 26:8.title: Psalms 26:8
Psalms 26:8.content: the habitation of thy house—where Thy house rests, as the tabernacle was not yet permanently fixed. honour dwelleth—conveys an allusion to the Holy of Holies.

Psalms 26:9.title: Psalms 26:9
Psalms 26:9.content: Gather not, &c.—Bring me not to death. bloody men—(compare Ps 5:6).

Psalms 26:10.title: Psalms 26:10
Psalms 26:10.content: Their whole conduct is that of violence and fraud.

Psalms 26:11.title: Psalms 26:11-12
Psalms 26:11.content: But, &c.—He contrasts his character and destiny with that of the wicked (compare Ps 26:1, 2).

Psalms 26:12.title: Psalms 26:11-12
Psalms 26:12.content: But, &c.—He contrasts his character and destiny with that of the wicked (compare Ps 26:1, 2).

Psalms 26:12.title: Psalms 26:12
Psalms 26:12.content: even place—free from occasions of stumbling—safety in his course is denoted. Hence he will render to God his praise publicly.

Psalms 27:1.title: Psalms 27:1
Psalms 27:1.content: light—is a common figure for comfort. strength—or, "stronghold"—affording security against all violence. The interrogations give greater vividness to the negation implied.

Psalms 27:2.title: Psalms 27:2
Psalms 27:2.content: eat … my flesh—(Job 19:22; Ps 14:4). The allusion to wild beasts illustrates their rapacity. they stumbled—"they" is emphatic; not I, but they were destroyed.

Psalms 27:3.title: Psalms 27:3
Psalms 27:3.content: In the greatest dangers. in this—that is, then, in such extremity.

Psalms 27:4.title: Psalms 27:4-5
Psalms 27:4.content: The secret of his confidence is his delight in communion with God (Ps 16:11; 23:6), beholding the harmony of His perfections, and seeking His favor in His temple or palace; a term applicable to the tabernacle (compare Ps 5:7). There he is safe (Ps 31:21; 61:5). The figure is changed in the last clause, but the sentiment is the same.

Psalms 27:5.title: Psalms 27:4-5
Psalms 27:5.content: The secret of his confidence is his delight in communion with God (Ps 16:11; 23:6), beholding the harmony of His perfections, and seeking His favor in His temple or palace; a term applicable to the tabernacle (compare Ps 5:7). There he is safe (Ps 31:21; 61:5). The figure is changed in the last clause, but the sentiment is the same.

Psalms 27:6.title: Psalms 27:6
Psalms 27:6.content: head be lifted up—I shall be placed beyond the reach of my enemies. Hence he avows his purpose of rendering joyful thank offerings.

Psalms 27:7.title: Psalms 27:7
Psalms 27:7.content: Still pressing need extorts prayer for help. cry with my voice—denotes earnestness. Other things equal, Christians in earnest pray audibly, even in secret.

Psalms 27:8.title: Psalms 27:8
Psalms 27:8.content: The meaning is clear, though the construction in a literal translation is obscure. The English Version supplies the implied clause. To seek God's face is to seek His favor (Ps 105:4).

Psalms 27:9.title: Psalms 27:9
Psalms 27:9.content: Hide not, &c.—(Ps 4:6; 22:24). Against rejection he pleads former mercy and love.

Psalms 27:10.title: Psalms 27:10
Psalms 27:10.content: In the extremity of earthly destitution (Ps 31:11; 38:11), God provides (compare Mt 25:35).

Psalms 27:11.title: Psalms 27:11
Psalms 27:11.content: thy way—of providence. a plain path—(Ps 26:12). enemies—literally, "watchers for my fall" (Ps 5:8).

Psalms 27:12.title: Psalms 27:12
Psalms 27:12.content: will—literally, "soul," "desire" (Ps 35:25). enemies—literally, "oppressors." Falsehood aids cruelty against him. breathe out—as being filled with it (Ac 9:1).

Psalms 27:13.title: Psalms 27:13
Psalms 27:13.content: The strong emotion is indicated by the incomplete sentence, for which the English Version supplies a proper clause; or, omitting that, and rendering, "yet I believed," &c., the contrast of his faith and his danger is expressed. to see—is to experience (Ps 22:17).

Psalms 27:14.title: Psalms 27:14
Psalms 27:14.content: Wait, &c.—in confident expectation. The last clause is, literally, "and wait," &c., as if expecting new measures of help.

Psalms 28:1.title: Psalms 28:1
Psalms 28:1.content: my rock—(Ps 18:2, 31). be not silent to me—literally, "from me," deaf or inattentive. become like them, &c.—share their fate. go down into the pit—or, "grave" (Ps 30:3).

Psalms 28:2.title: Psalms 28:2
Psalms 28:2.content: lift up my hands—a gesture of prayer (Ps 63:4; 141:2). oracle—place of speaking (Ex 25:22; Nu 7:89), where God answered His people (compare Ps 5:7).

Psalms 28:3.title: Psalms 28:3
Psalms 28:3.content: Draw me not away—implies punishment as well as death (compare Ps 26:9). Hypocrisy is the special wickedness mentioned.

Psalms 28:4.title: Psalms 28:4
Psalms 28:4.content: The imprecation is justified in Ps 28:5. The force of the passage is greatly enhanced by the accumulation of terms describing their sin. endeavours—points out their deliberate sinfulness.

Psalms 28:5.title: Psalms 28:5
Psalms 28:5.content: Disregard of God's judgments brings a righteous punishment. destroy … build … up—The positive strengthened by the negative form.

Psalms 28:7.title: Psalms 28:7
Psalms 28:7.content: The repetition of "heart" denotes his sincerity.

Psalms 28:8.title: Psalms 28:8
Psalms 28:8.content: The distinction made between the people. their strength—and the anointed—may indicate Absalom's rebellion as the occasion.

Psalms 28:9.title: Psalms 28:9
Psalms 28:9.content: The special prayer for the people sustains this view. feed them—as a shepherd (Ps 23:1, &c.).

Psalms 29:1.title: Psalms 29:1
Psalms 29:1.content: Give—or, "ascribe" (De 32:3). mighty—or, "sons of the mighty" (Ps 89:6). Heavenly beings, as angels.

Psalms 29:2.title: Psalms 29:2
Psalms 29:2.content: name—as (Ps 5:11; 8:1). beauty of holiness—the loveliness of a spiritual worship, of which the perceptible beauty of the sanctuary worship was but a type.

Psalms 29:3.title: Psalms 29:3
Psalms 29:3.content: The voice of the Lord—audible exhibition of His power in the tempest, of which thunder is a specimen, but not the uniform or sole example. the waters—the clouds or vapors (Ps 18:11; Jer 10:13).

Psalms 29:5.title: Psalms 29:5-6
Psalms 29:5.content: The tall and large cedars, especially of Lebanon, are shivered, utterly broken. The waving of the mountain forests before the wind is expressed by the figure of skipping or leaping.

Psalms 29:6.title: Psalms 29:5-6
Psalms 29:6.content: The tall and large cedars, especially of Lebanon, are shivered, utterly broken. The waving of the mountain forests before the wind is expressed by the figure of skipping or leaping.

Psalms 29:7.title: Psalms 29:7
Psalms 29:7.content: divideth—literally, "hews off." The lightning, like flakes and splinters hewed from stone or wood, flies through the air.

Psalms 29:8.title: Psalms 29:8
Psalms 29:8.content: the wilderness—especially Kadesh, south of Judea, is selected as another scene of this display of divine power, as a vast and desolate region impresses the mind, like mountains, with images of grandeur.

Psalms 29:9.title: Psalms 29:9
Psalms 29:9.content: Terror-stricken animals and denuded forests close the illustration. In view of this scene of awful sublimity, God's worshippers respond to the call of Ps 29:2, and speak or cry, "Glory!" By "temple," or "palace" (God's residence, Ps 5:7), may here be meant heaven, or the whole frame of nature, as the angels are called on for praise.

Psalms 29:10.title: Psalms 29:10-11
Psalms 29:10.content: Over this terrible raging of the elements God is enthroned, directing and restraining by sovereign power; and hence the comfort of His people. "This awful God is ours, our Father and our Love."

Psalms 29:11.title: Psalms 29:10-11
Psalms 29:11.content: Over this terrible raging of the elements God is enthroned, directing and restraining by sovereign power; and hence the comfort of His people. "This awful God is ours, our Father and our Love."

Psalms 30:1.title: Psalms 30:1
Psalms 30:1.content: lifted me up—as one is drawn from a well (Ps 40:2).

Psalms 30:2.title: Psalms 30:2
Psalms 30:2.content: healed me—Affliction is often described as disease (Ps 6:2; 41:4; 107:20), and so relief by healing.

Psalms 30:3.title: Psalms 30:3
Psalms 30:3.content: The terms describe extreme danger. soul—or, "myself." grave—literally, "hell," as in Ps 16:10. hast kept me … pit—quickened or revived me from the state of dying (compare Ps 28:1).

Psalms 30:4.title: Psalms 30:4
Psalms 30:4.content: remembrance—the thing remembered or memorial. holiness—as the sum of God's perfections (compare Ps 22:3), used as name (Ex 3:15; Ps 135:13).

Psalms 30:5.title: Psalms 30:5
Psalms 30:5.content: Relatively, the longest experience of divine anger by the pious is momentary. These precious words have consoled millions.

Psalms 30:6.title: Psalms 30:6-7
Psalms 30:6.content: What particular prosperity is meant we do not know; perhaps his accession to the throne. In his self-complacent elation he was checked by God's hiding His face (compare Ps 22:24; 27:9).

Psalms 30:7.title: Psalms 30:6-7
Psalms 30:7.content: What particular prosperity is meant we do not know; perhaps his accession to the throne. In his self-complacent elation he was checked by God's hiding His face (compare Ps 22:24; 27:9).

Psalms 30:8.title: Psalms 30:8-11
Psalms 30:8.content: As in Ps 6:5; 88:10; Isa 38:18, the appeal for mercy is based on the destruction of his agency in praising God here, which death would produce. The terms expressing relief are poetical, and not to be pressed, though "dancing" is the translation of a word which means a lute, whose cheerful notes are contrasted with mourning, or (Am 5:16) wailing.

Psalms 30:9.title: Psalms 30:8-11
Psalms 30:9.content: As in Ps 6:5; 88:10; Isa 38:18, the appeal for mercy is based on the destruction of his agency in praising God here, which death would produce. The terms expressing relief are poetical, and not to be pressed, though "dancing" is the translation of a word which means a lute, whose cheerful notes are contrasted with mourning, or (Am 5:16) wailing.

Psalms 30:10.title: Psalms 30:8-11
Psalms 30:10.content: As in Ps 6:5; 88:10; Isa 38:18, the appeal for mercy is based on the destruction of his agency in praising God here, which death would produce. The terms expressing relief are poetical, and not to be pressed, though "dancing" is the translation of a word which means a lute, whose cheerful notes are contrasted with mourning, or (Am 5:16) wailing.

Psalms 30:11.title: Psalms 30:8-11
Psalms 30:11.content: As in Ps 6:5; 88:10; Isa 38:18, the appeal for mercy is based on the destruction of his agency in praising God here, which death would produce. The terms expressing relief are poetical, and not to be pressed, though "dancing" is the translation of a word which means a lute, whose cheerful notes are contrasted with mourning, or (Am 5:16) wailing.

Psalms 30:11.title: Psalms 30:11
Psalms 30:11.content: sackcloth—was used, even by kings, in distress (1Ch 21:16; Isa 37:1) but "gladness," used for a garment, shows the language to be figurative.

Psalms 30:12.title: Psalms 30:12
Psalms 30:12.content: Though "my" is supplied before "glory" it is better as in Ps 16:9, to receive it as used for tongue, the organ of praise. The ultimate end of God's mercies to us is our praise to Him.

Psalms 31:1.title: Psalms 31:1
Psalms 31:1.content: Expresses the general tone of feeling of the Psalm.

Psalms 31:2.title: Psalms 31:2-4
Psalms 31:2.content: He seeks help in God's righteous government (Ps 5:8), and begs for an attentive hearing, and speedy and effectual aid. With no other help and no claim of merit, he relies solely on God's regard to His own perfections for a safe guidance and release from the snares of his enemies. On the terms "rock," &c., (compare Ps 17:2; 18:2, 50; 20:6; 23:3; 25:21).

Psalms 31:3.title: Psalms 31:2-4
Psalms 31:3.content: He seeks help in God's righteous government (Ps 5:8), and begs for an attentive hearing, and speedy and effectual aid. With no other help and no claim of merit, he relies solely on God's regard to His own perfections for a safe guidance and release from the snares of his enemies. On the terms "rock," &c., (compare Ps 17:2; 18:2, 50; 20:6; 23:3; 25:21).

Psalms 31:4.title: Psalms 31:2-4
Psalms 31:4.content: He seeks help in God's righteous government (Ps 5:8), and begs for an attentive hearing, and speedy and effectual aid. With no other help and no claim of merit, he relies solely on God's regard to His own perfections for a safe guidance and release from the snares of his enemies. On the terms "rock," &c., (compare Ps 17:2; 18:2, 50; 20:6; 23:3; 25:21).

Psalms 31:5.title: Psalms 31:5-6
Psalms 31:5.content: commit my spirit—my life, or myself. Our Saviour used the words on the Cross [Lu 23:46], not as prophetical, but, as many pious men have done, as expressive of His unshaken confidence in God. The Psalmist rests on God's faithfulness to His promises to His people, and hence avows himself one of them, detesting all who revere objects of idolatry (compare De 32:21; 1Co 8:4).

Psalms 31:6.title: Psalms 31:5-6
Psalms 31:6.content: commit my spirit—my life, or myself. Our Saviour used the words on the Cross [Lu 23:46], not as prophetical, but, as many pious men have done, as expressive of His unshaken confidence in God. The Psalmist rests on God's faithfulness to His promises to His people, and hence avows himself one of them, detesting all who revere objects of idolatry (compare De 32:21; 1Co 8:4).

Psalms 31:7.title: Psalms 31:7
Psalms 31:7.content: hast known my soul, &c.—had regard to me in trouble.

Psalms 31:8.title: Psalms 31:8
Psalms 31:8.content: shut me up … enemy—abandon to (1Sa 23:11). large room—place of safety (compare Ps 18:19).

Psalms 31:9.title: Psalms 31:9-10
Psalms 31:9.content: mine eye, &c.—denotes extreme weakness (compare Ps 6:7). grief—mingled sorrow and indignation (Ps 6:7). soul and … belly—the whole person.

Psalms 31:10.title: Psalms 31:9-10
Psalms 31:10.content: mine eye, &c.—denotes extreme weakness (compare Ps 6:7). grief—mingled sorrow and indignation (Ps 6:7). soul and … belly—the whole person.

Psalms 31:10.title: Psalms 31:10
Psalms 31:10.content: Though the effects ascribed to grief are not mere figures of speech— spent … consumed—must be taken in the modified sense of wasted and decayed. iniquity—or, suffering by it (see on Ps 40:12).

Psalms 31:11.title: Psalms 31:11
Psalms 31:11.content: among—or, literally, "from," or, "by" my enemies. The latter clauses describe the progress of his disgrace to the lowest degree, till,

Psalms 31:12.title: Psalms 31:12
Psalms 31:12.content: he is forgotten as one dead, and contemned as a useless broken vessel.

Psalms 31:13.title: Psalms 31:13
Psalms 31:13.content: For—introduces further reasons for his prayer, the unjust, deliberate, and murderous purposes of his foes.

Psalms 31:14.title: Psalms 31:14-18
Psalms 31:14.content: In his profession of trust he includes the terms of the prayer expressing it.

Psalms 31:15.title: Psalms 31:14-18
Psalms 31:15.content: In his profession of trust he includes the terms of the prayer expressing it.

Psalms 31:15.title: Psalms 31:15
Psalms 31:15.content: times—course of life. deliver … hand—opposed to "shut me up," &c., of Ps 31:8.

Psalms 31:16.title: Psalms 31:14-18
Psalms 31:16.content: In his profession of trust he includes the terms of the prayer expressing it.

Psalms 31:16.title: Psalms 31:16
Psalms 31:16.content: Make … shine—(Compare Nu 6:25; Ps 4:6). Deprecating from himself, he imprecates on the wicked God's displeasure, and prays that their virulent persecution of him may be stopped.

Psalms 31:17.title: Psalms 31:14-18
Psalms 31:17.content: In his profession of trust he includes the terms of the prayer expressing it.

Psalms 31:18.title: Psalms 31:14-18
Psalms 31:18.content: In his profession of trust he includes the terms of the prayer expressing it.

Psalms 31:19.title: Psalms 31:19-21
Psalms 31:19.content: God displays openly His purposed goodness to His people.

Psalms 31:20.title: Psalms 31:19-21
Psalms 31:20.content: God displays openly His purposed goodness to His people.

Psalms 31:20.title: Psalms 31:20
Psalms 31:20.content: the secret of thy presence—or, covering of Thy countenance; the protection He thus affords; compare Ps 27:5 for a similar figure; "dwelling" used there for "presence" here. The idea of security further presented by the figure of a tent and a fortified city [Ps 31:21].

Psalms 31:21.title: Psalms 31:19-21
Psalms 31:21.content: God displays openly His purposed goodness to His people.

Psalms 31:22.title: Psalms 31:22
Psalms 31:22.content: For I said—literally, "And I said," in an adversative sense. I, thus favored, was despondent. in my haste—in my terror. cut off … eyes—from all the protection of Thy presence.

Psalms 31:23.title: Psalms 31:23-24
Psalms 31:23.content: the Lord … proud doer—literally, "the Lord is keeping faith," that is, with His people, and is repaying, &c. Then let none despair, but take courage; their hopes shall not be in vain.

Psalms 31:24.title: Psalms 31:23-24
Psalms 31:24.content: the Lord … proud doer—literally, "the Lord is keeping faith," that is, with His people, and is repaying, &c. Then let none despair, but take courage; their hopes shall not be in vain.

Psalms 32:1.title: Psalms 32:1-2
Psalms 32:1.content: (Compare Ro 4:6). forgiven—literally, "taken away," opposed to retain (Joh 20:23). covered—so that God no longer regards the sin (Ps 85:3).

Psalms 32:2.title: Psalms 32:1-2
Psalms 32:2.content: (Compare Ro 4:6). forgiven—literally, "taken away," opposed to retain (Joh 20:23). covered—so that God no longer regards the sin (Ps 85:3).

Psalms 32:2.title: Psalms 32:2
Psalms 32:2.content: imputeth—charge to him, and treat him accordingly. no guile—or, deceit, no false estimate of himself, nor insincerity before God (compare Ro 8:1).

Psalms 32:3.title: Psalms 32:3-4
Psalms 32:3.content: A vivid description of felt, but unacknowledged, sin. When—literally, "for," as in Ps 32:4.

Psalms 32:4.title: Psalms 32:3-4
Psalms 32:4.content: A vivid description of felt, but unacknowledged, sin. When—literally, "for," as in Ps 32:4.

Psalms 32:4.title: Psalms 32:4
Psalms 32:4.content: thy hand—of God, or power in distressing him (Ps 38:2). moisture—vital juices of the body, the parching heat of which expresses the anguish of the soul. On the other figures, compare Ps 6:2, 7; 31:9-11. If composed on the occasion of the fifty-first Psalm, this distress may have been protracted for several months.

Psalms 32:5.title: Psalms 32:5
Psalms 32:5.content: A prompt fulfilment of the purposed confession is followed by a prompt forgiveness.

Psalms 32:6.title: Psalms 32:6
Psalms 32:6.content: For this—that is, my happy experience. godly—pious in the sense of Ps 4:3. a time—(Isa 55:6); when God's Spirit inclines us to seek pardon, He is ready to forgive. floods, &c.—denotes great danger (Ps 18:17; 66:12).

Psalms 32:7.title: Psalms 32:7
Psalms 32:7.content: His experience illustrates the statement of Ps 32:6.

Psalms 32:8.title: Psalms 32:8
Psalms 32:8.content: Whether, as most likely, the language of David (compare Ps 51:13), or that of God, this is a promise of divine guidance. I will … mine eye—or, My eye shall be on thee, watching and directing thy way.

Psalms 32:9.title: Psalms 32:9
Psalms 32:9.content: The latter clause, more literally, "in that they come not near thee"; that is, because they will not come, &c., unless forced by bit and bridle.

Psalms 32:10.title: Psalms 32:10
Psalms 32:10.content: The sorrows of the impenitent contrasted with the peace and safety secured by God's mercy.

Psalms 32:11.title: Psalms 32:11
Psalms 32:11.content: The righteous and upright, or those conforming to the divine teaching for securing the divine blessing, may well rejoice with shouting.

Psalms 33:1.title: Psalms 33:1-3
Psalms 33:1.content: The sentiment falls in with Ps 32:11 (compare 1Co 14:15). The instruments (Ps 92:3; 144:9) do not exclude the voice.

Psalms 33:2.title: Psalms 33:1-3
Psalms 33:2.content: The sentiment falls in with Ps 32:11 (compare 1Co 14:15). The instruments (Ps 92:3; 144:9) do not exclude the voice.

Psalms 33:3.title: Psalms 33:1-3
Psalms 33:3.content: The sentiment falls in with Ps 32:11 (compare 1Co 14:15). The instruments (Ps 92:3; 144:9) do not exclude the voice.

Psalms 33:3.title: Psalms 33:3
Psalms 33:3.content: a new song—fresh, adapted to the occasion (Ps 40:3; 96:1). play skilfully—(Compare 1Sa 16:17).

Psalms 33:4.title: Psalms 33:4-9
Psalms 33:4.content: Reasons for praise: first, God's truth, faithfulness, and mercy, generally; then, His creative power which all must honor.

Psalms 33:5.title: Psalms 33:4-9
Psalms 33:5.content: Reasons for praise: first, God's truth, faithfulness, and mercy, generally; then, His creative power which all must honor.

Psalms 33:6.title: Psalms 33:4-9
Psalms 33:6.content: Reasons for praise: first, God's truth, faithfulness, and mercy, generally; then, His creative power which all must honor.

Psalms 33:6.title: Psalms 33:6
Psalms 33:6.content: In "word" and "breath"—or, "spirit," there may be an allusion to the Son (Joh 1:1) and Holy Spirit.

Psalms 33:7.title: Psalms 33:4-9
Psalms 33:7.content: Reasons for praise: first, God's truth, faithfulness, and mercy, generally; then, His creative power which all must honor.

Psalms 33:8.title: Psalms 33:4-9
Psalms 33:8.content: Reasons for praise: first, God's truth, faithfulness, and mercy, generally; then, His creative power which all must honor.

Psalms 33:9.title: Psalms 33:4-9
Psalms 33:9.content: Reasons for praise: first, God's truth, faithfulness, and mercy, generally; then, His creative power which all must honor.

Psalms 33:9.title: Psalms 33:9
Psalms 33:9.content: he spake—literally, "said." it was—The addition of "done" weakens the sense (compare Ge 1:3-10).

Psalms 33:10.title: Psalms 33:10-11
Psalms 33:10.content: In God's providence He thwarts men's purposes and executes His own. heathen—literally, "nations."

Psalms 33:11.title: Psalms 33:10-11
Psalms 33:11.content: In God's providence He thwarts men's purposes and executes His own. heathen—literally, "nations."

Psalms 33:12.title: Psalms 33:12-19
Psalms 33:12.content: The inference from the foregoing in Ps 33:12 is illustrated by God's special providence, underlying which is His minute knowledge of all men.

Psalms 33:13.title: Psalms 33:12-19
Psalms 33:13.content: The inference from the foregoing in Ps 33:12 is illustrated by God's special providence, underlying which is His minute knowledge of all men.

Psalms 33:14.title: Psalms 33:12-19
Psalms 33:14.content: The inference from the foregoing in Ps 33:12 is illustrated by God's special providence, underlying which is His minute knowledge of all men.

Psalms 33:15.title: Psalms 33:12-19
Psalms 33:15.content: The inference from the foregoing in Ps 33:12 is illustrated by God's special providence, underlying which is His minute knowledge of all men.

Psalms 33:15.title: Psalms 33:15
Psalms 33:15.content: fashioneth—or, "forms," and hence knows and controls (Pr 21:1). alike—without exception. considereth—or, "understands"; God knows men's motives.

Psalms 33:16.title: Psalms 33:12-19
Psalms 33:16.content: The inference from the foregoing in Ps 33:12 is illustrated by God's special providence, underlying which is His minute knowledge of all men.

Psalms 33:16.title: Psalms 33:16-17
Psalms 33:16.content: Men's usual reliances in their greatest exigencies are, in themselves, useless.

Psalms 33:17.title: Psalms 33:12-19
Psalms 33:17.content: The inference from the foregoing in Ps 33:12 is illustrated by God's special providence, underlying which is His minute knowledge of all men.

Psalms 33:17.title: Psalms 33:16-17
Psalms 33:17.content: Men's usual reliances in their greatest exigencies are, in themselves, useless.

Psalms 33:17.title: Psalms 33:17
Psalms 33:17.content: On the war horse (compare Job 39:19-25). a vain thing—a lie, which deceives us.

Psalms 33:18.title: Psalms 33:12-19
Psalms 33:18.content: The inference from the foregoing in Ps 33:12 is illustrated by God's special providence, underlying which is His minute knowledge of all men.

Psalms 33:18.title: Psalms 33:18-19
Psalms 33:18.content: Contrasted is God's guidance and power to save from the greatest earthly evil and its most painful precursor, and hence from all.

Psalms 33:19.title: Psalms 33:12-19
Psalms 33:19.content: The inference from the foregoing in Ps 33:12 is illustrated by God's special providence, underlying which is His minute knowledge of all men.

Psalms 33:19.title: Psalms 33:18-19
Psalms 33:19.content: Contrasted is God's guidance and power to save from the greatest earthly evil and its most painful precursor, and hence from all.

Psalms 33:21.title: Psalms 33:21
Psalms 33:21.content: his holy name—(Compare Ps 5:12; 22:22; 30:4). Our faith measures mercy (Mt 9:29); and if of grace, it is no more of debt (Ro 11:6).

Psalms 34:1.title: Psalms 34:1-4
Psalms 34:1.content: Even in distress, which excites supplication, there is always matter for praising and thanking God (compare Eph 5:20; Php 4:6).

Psalms 34:2.title: Psalms 34:1-4
Psalms 34:2.content: Even in distress, which excites supplication, there is always matter for praising and thanking God (compare Eph 5:20; Php 4:6).

Psalms 34:2.title: Psalms 34:2
Psalms 34:2.content: make her boast—"glory" (Ps 105:3; compare Ga 6:14). humble—"the pious," as in Ps 9:12; 25:9.

Psalms 34:3.title: Psalms 34:1-4
Psalms 34:3.content: Even in distress, which excites supplication, there is always matter for praising and thanking God (compare Eph 5:20; Php 4:6).

Psalms 34:3.title: Psalms 34:3
Psalms 34:3.content: magnify the Lord—ascribe greatness to Him, an act of praise. together—"alike" (Ps 33:15), or, equally, without exception.

Psalms 34:4.title: Psalms 34:1-4
Psalms 34:4.content: Even in distress, which excites supplication, there is always matter for praising and thanking God (compare Eph 5:20; Php 4:6).

Psalms 34:4.title: Psalms 34:4
Psalms 34:4.content: delivered … fears—as well as actual evil (Ps 64:1).

Psalms 34:5.title: Psalms 34:5-7
Psalms 34:5.content: God's favor to the pious generally, and to himself specially, is celebrated. looked—with desire for help. lightened—or, "brightened," expressing joy, opposed to the downcast features of those who are ashamed or disappointed (Ps 25:2, 3).

Psalms 34:6.title: Psalms 34:5-7
Psalms 34:6.content: God's favor to the pious generally, and to himself specially, is celebrated. looked—with desire for help. lightened—or, "brightened," expressing joy, opposed to the downcast features of those who are ashamed or disappointed (Ps 25:2, 3).

Psalms 34:6.title: Psalms 34:6
Psalms 34:6.content: This poor man—literally, "humble," himself as a specimen of such.

Psalms 34:7.title: Psalms 34:5-7
Psalms 34:7.content: God's favor to the pious generally, and to himself specially, is celebrated. looked—with desire for help. lightened—or, "brightened," expressing joy, opposed to the downcast features of those who are ashamed or disappointed (Ps 25:2, 3).

Psalms 34:7.title: Psalms 34:7
Psalms 34:7.content: angel—of the covenant (Isa 63:9), of whom as a leader of God's host (Jos 5:14; 1Ki 22:19), the phrase— encampeth, &c.—is appropriate; or, "angel" used collectively for angels (Heb 1:14).

Psalms 34:9.title: Psalms 34:9
Psalms 34:9.content: that fear him—who are pious—fear and love (Pr 1:7; 9:10). saints—consecrated to His service (Isa 40:31).

Psalms 34:10.title: Psalms 34:10
Psalms 34:10.content: not want any good—"good" is emphatic; they may be afflicted (compare Ps 34:10); but this may be a good (2Co 4:17, 18; Heb 12:10, 11).

Psalms 34:12.title: Psalms 34:12
Psalms 34:12.content: What man—Whoever desires the blessings of piety, let him attend.

Psalms 34:13.title: Psalms 34:13-14
Psalms 34:13.content: Sins of thought included in those of speech (Lu 6:45), avoiding evil and doing good in our relations to men are based on a right relation to God.

Psalms 34:14.title: Psalms 34:13-14
Psalms 34:14.content: Sins of thought included in those of speech (Lu 6:45), avoiding evil and doing good in our relations to men are based on a right relation to God.

Psalms 34:15.title: Psalms 34:15
Psalms 34:15.content: eyes of the Lord are upon—(Ps 32:8; 33:18).

Psalms 34:16.title: Psalms 34:16
Psalms 34:16.content: face … against—opposed to them (Le 17:10; 20:3). cut off the remembrance—utterly destroy (Ps 109:13).

Psalms 34:17.title: Psalms 34:17-18
Psalms 34:17.content: Humble penitents are objects of God's special tender regard (Ps 51:19; Isa 57:15).

Psalms 34:18.title: Psalms 34:17-18
Psalms 34:18.content: Humble penitents are objects of God's special tender regard (Ps 51:19; Isa 57:15).

Psalms 34:21.title: Psalms 34:21-22
Psalms 34:21.content: Contrast in the destiny of righteous and wicked; the former shall be delivered and never come into condemnation (Joh 5:24; Ro 8:1); the latter are left under condemnation and desolate.

Psalms 34:22.title: Psalms 34:21-22
Psalms 34:22.content: Contrast in the destiny of righteous and wicked; the former shall be delivered and never come into condemnation (Joh 5:24; Ro 8:1); the latter are left under condemnation and desolate.

Psalms 35:1.title: Psalms 35:1-3
Psalms 35:1.content: God is invoked in the character of a warrior (Ex 15:3; De 32:41).

Psalms 35:2.title: Psalms 35:1-3
Psalms 35:2.content: God is invoked in the character of a warrior (Ex 15:3; De 32:41).

Psalms 35:3.title: Psalms 35:1-3
Psalms 35:3.content: God is invoked in the character of a warrior (Ex 15:3; De 32:41).

Psalms 35:3.title: Psalms 35:3
Psalms 35:3.content: fight against—literally, "devour my devourers." stop the way against—literally, "shut up" (the way), to meet or oppose, &c. I … thy salvation—who saves thee.

Psalms 35:4.title: Psalms 35:4
Psalms 35:4.content: (Compare Ps 9:17). devise my hurt—purpose for evil to me.

Psalms 35:5.title: Psalms 35:5-6
Psalms 35:5.content: (Compare Ps 1:4)—a terrible fate; driven by wind on a slippery path in darkness, and hotly pursued by supernatural violence (2Sa 24:16; Ac 12:23).

Psalms 35:6.title: Psalms 35:5-6
Psalms 35:6.content: (Compare Ps 1:4)—a terrible fate; driven by wind on a slippery path in darkness, and hotly pursued by supernatural violence (2Sa 24:16; Ac 12:23).

Psalms 35:7.title: Psalms 35:7-8
Psalms 35:7.content: net in a pit—or, "pit of their net"—or, "net-pit," as "holy hill" for "hill of holiness" (Ps 2:6); a figure from hunting (Ps 7:15). Their imprecations on impenitent rebels against God need no vindication; His justice and wrath are for such; His mercy for penitents. Compare Ps 7:16; 11:5, on the peculiar fate of the wicked here noticed.

Psalms 35:8.title: Psalms 35:7-8
Psalms 35:8.content: net in a pit—or, "pit of their net"—or, "net-pit," as "holy hill" for "hill of holiness" (Ps 2:6); a figure from hunting (Ps 7:15). Their imprecations on impenitent rebels against God need no vindication; His justice and wrath are for such; His mercy for penitents. Compare Ps 7:16; 11:5, on the peculiar fate of the wicked here noticed.

Psalms 35:10.title: Psalms 35:10
Psalms 35:10.content: All my bones—every part. him that spoileth him—(Compare Ps 10:2).

Psalms 35:11.title: Psalms 35:11
Psalms 35:11.content: False witnesses—literally, "Witnesses of injustice and cruelty" (compare Ps 11:5; 25:19).

Psalms 35:12.title: Psalms 35:12-14
Psalms 35:12.content: Though they rendered evil for good, he showed a tender sympathy in their affliction. spoiling—literally, "bereavement." The usual modes of showing grief are made, as figures, to express his sorrow.

Psalms 35:13.title: Psalms 35:12-14
Psalms 35:13.content: Though they rendered evil for good, he showed a tender sympathy in their affliction. spoiling—literally, "bereavement." The usual modes of showing grief are made, as figures, to express his sorrow.

Psalms 35:13.title: Psalms 35:13
Psalms 35:13.content: prayer … bosom—may denote either the posture—the head bowed—(compare 1Ki 18:42)—or, that the prayer was in secret. Some think there is a reference to the result—the prayer would benefit him if not them.

Psalms 35:14.title: Psalms 35:12-14
Psalms 35:14.content: Though they rendered evil for good, he showed a tender sympathy in their affliction. spoiling—literally, "bereavement." The usual modes of showing grief are made, as figures, to express his sorrow.

Psalms 35:14.title: Psalms 35:14
Psalms 35:14.content: behaved—literally, "went on"—denoting his habit. heavily—or, "squalidly," his sorrowing occasioning neglect of his person. Altogether, his grief was that of one for a dearly loved relative.

Psalms 35:15.title: Psalms 35:15-16
Psalms 35:15.content: On the contrary, they rejoiced in his affliction. Halting, or, "lameness," as in Ps 38:17 for any distress. abjects—either as cripples (compare 2Sa 4:4), contemptible; or, degraded persons, such as had been beaten (compare Job 30:1-8). I knew it not—either the persons, or, reasons of such conduct. tear me, and ceased not—literally, "were not silent"—showing that the tearing meant slandering.

Psalms 35:16.title: Psalms 35:15-16
Psalms 35:16.content: On the contrary, they rejoiced in his affliction. Halting, or, "lameness," as in Ps 38:17 for any distress. abjects—either as cripples (compare 2Sa 4:4), contemptible; or, degraded persons, such as had been beaten (compare Job 30:1-8). I knew it not—either the persons, or, reasons of such conduct. tear me, and ceased not—literally, "were not silent"—showing that the tearing meant slandering.

Psalms 35:16.title: Psalms 35:16
Psalms 35:16.content: mockers—who were hired to make sport at feasts (Pr 28:21).

Psalms 35:19.title: Psalms 35:19
Psalms 35:19.content: enemies wrongfully—by false and slanderous imputations. wink with the eye—an insulting gesture (Pr 6:13). without a cause—manifests more malice than having a wrong cause.

Psalms 35:20.title: Psalms 35:20
Psalms 35:20.content: deceitful matters—or, "words of deceit." quiet in the land—the pious lovers of peace.

Psalms 35:21.title: Psalms 35:21
Psalms 35:21.content: On the gesture compare Ps 22:7; and on the expressions of malicious triumph, compare Ps 10:13; 28:3.

Psalms 35:23.title: Psalms 35:23-24
Psalms 35:23.content: (Compare Ps 7:6; 26:1; 2Th 1:6). God's righteous government is the hope of the pious and terror of the wicked.

Psalms 35:24.title: Psalms 35:23-24
Psalms 35:24.content: (Compare Ps 7:6; 26:1; 2Th 1:6). God's righteous government is the hope of the pious and terror of the wicked.

Psalms 35:25.title: Psalms 35:25
Psalms 35:25.content: swallowed him up—utterly destroyed him (Ps 21:9; La 2:16).

Psalms 35:27.title: Psalms 35:27
Psalms 35:27.content: favour … cause—delight in it, as vindicated by Thee. Let the Lord, &c.—Let Him be greatly praised for His care of the just.

Psalms 35:28.title: Psalms 35:28
Psalms 35:28.content: In this praise of God's equitable government (Ps 5:8) the writer promises ever to engage.

Psalms 36:1.title: Psalms 36:1
Psalms 36:1.content: The general sense of this difficult verse is, "that the wicked have no fear of God." The first clause may be rendered, "Saith transgression in my heart, in respect to the wicked, there is no fear," &c., that is, such is my reflection on men's transgressions.

Psalms 36:2.title: Psalms 36:2-4
Psalms 36:2.content: This reflection detailed. until his iniquity—literally, "for finding his iniquity for hating"; that is, he persuades himself God will not so find it—"for hating" involving the idea of punishing. Hence his words of iniquity and deceit, and his bold rejection of all right principles of conduct. The climax is that he deliberately adopts and patronizes evil. The negative forms affirm more emphatically their contraries.

Psalms 36:3.title: Psalms 36:2-4
Psalms 36:3.content: This reflection detailed. until his iniquity—literally, "for finding his iniquity for hating"; that is, he persuades himself God will not so find it—"for hating" involving the idea of punishing. Hence his words of iniquity and deceit, and his bold rejection of all right principles of conduct. The climax is that he deliberately adopts and patronizes evil. The negative forms affirm more emphatically their contraries.

Psalms 36:4.title: Psalms 36:2-4
Psalms 36:4.content: This reflection detailed. until his iniquity—literally, "for finding his iniquity for hating"; that is, he persuades himself God will not so find it—"for hating" involving the idea of punishing. Hence his words of iniquity and deceit, and his bold rejection of all right principles of conduct. The climax is that he deliberately adopts and patronizes evil. The negative forms affirm more emphatically their contraries.

Psalms 36:5.title: Psalms 36:5-6
Psalms 36:5.content: mercy … and … faithfulness—as mercy and truth (Ps 25:10).

Psalms 36:6.title: Psalms 36:5-6
Psalms 36:6.content: mercy … and … faithfulness—as mercy and truth (Ps 25:10).

Psalms 36:6.title: Psalms 36:6
Psalms 36:6.content: righteousness [and] judgments—qualities of a good government (Ps 5:8; 31:1). These all are set forth, by the figures used, as unbounded.

Psalms 36:7.title: Psalms 36:7
Psalms 36:7.content: shadow of thy wings—(Compare De 32:11; Ps 91:1).

Psalms 36:8.title: Psalms 36:8
Psalms 36:8.content: fatness—richness. thy house—residence—for the privileges and blessings of communion with God (Ps 23:6; 27:4). river of thy pleasures—plenteous supply; may allude to Eden.

Psalms 36:9.title: Psalms 36:9
Psalms 36:9.content: Light is an emblem of all blessings, given of God as a means to gain more.

Psalms 36:10.title: Psalms 36:10
Psalms 36:10.content: that know thee—right knowledge of God is the source of right affections and conduct.

Psalms 36:11.title: Psalms 36:11
Psalms 36:11.content: foot of … hand … wicked—all kinds of violent dealing.

Psalms 36:12.title: Psalms 36:12
Psalms 36:12.content: There—in the acting of violence, they are overthrown. A signal defeat.

Psalms 37:1.title: Psalms 37:1-2
Psalms 37:1.content: The general sentiment of the whole Psalm is expressed. The righteous need not be vexed by the prosperity of the wicked; for it is transient, and their destiny undesirable.

Psalms 37:2.title: Psalms 37:1-2
Psalms 37:2.content: The general sentiment of the whole Psalm is expressed. The righteous need not be vexed by the prosperity of the wicked; for it is transient, and their destiny undesirable.

Psalms 37:3.title: Psalms 37:3
Psalms 37:3.content: Trust—sure of safety. shalt thou dwell—or, "dwell thou"; repose quietly. verily … fed—or, "feed on truth," God's promise (Ps 36:5; compare Ho 12:1).

Psalms 37:4.title: Psalms 37:4
Psalms 37:4.content: desires—(Ps 20:5; 21:2), what is lawful and right, really good (Ps 84:11).

Psalms 37:5.title: Psalms 37:5
Psalms 37:5.content: Commit thy way—(Pr 16:3). Works—what you have to do and cannot set forth as a burden. trust … in him—literally, "on Him." He will do what you cannot (compare Ps 22:8; 31:6). He will not suffer your character to remain under suspicion.

Psalms 37:7.title: Psalms 37:7-8
Psalms 37:7.content: Rest in—literally, "Be silent to the Lord." and wait—Be submissive—avoid petulance and murmurings, anger and rash doing.

Psalms 37:8.title: Psalms 37:7-8
Psalms 37:8.content: Rest in—literally, "Be silent to the Lord." and wait—Be submissive—avoid petulance and murmurings, anger and rash doing.

Psalms 37:9.title: Psalms 37:9
Psalms 37:9.content: Two reasons: The prosperity of the wicked is short; and the pious, by humble trust, will secure all covenant blessing, denoted here by "inherit the earth" (compare Ps 25:13).

Psalms 37:10.title: Psalms 37:10-11
Psalms 37:10.content: shall not be—literally, "is not"—is not to be found.

Psalms 37:11.title: Psalms 37:10-11
Psalms 37:11.content: shall not be—literally, "is not"—is not to be found.

Psalms 37:13.title: Psalms 37:13
Psalms 37:13.content: (Compare Ps 2:4). seeth—knows certainly. his day—of punishment, long delayed, shall yet come (Heb 10:37).

Psalms 37:14.title: Psalms 37:14-15
Psalms 37:14.content: sword, and … bow—for any instruments of violence. slay—literally, "slaughter" (1Sa 25:11). poor and needy—God's people (Ps 10:17; 12:5). The punishment of the wicked as drawn on themselves—often mentioned (compare Ps 7:15, 16; 35:8).

Psalms 37:15.title: Psalms 37:14-15
Psalms 37:15.content: sword, and … bow—for any instruments of violence. slay—literally, "slaughter" (1Sa 25:11). poor and needy—God's people (Ps 10:17; 12:5). The punishment of the wicked as drawn on themselves—often mentioned (compare Ps 7:15, 16; 35:8).

Psalms 37:16.title: Psalms 37:16
Psalms 37:16.content: riches—literally, "noise and tumult," as incidental to much wealth (compare Ps 39:6). Thus the contrast with the "little" of one man is more vivid.

Psalms 37:17.title: Psalms 37:17
Psalms 37:17.content: Even the members of the body needed to hold weapons are destroyed.

Psalms 37:18.title: Psalms 37:18-19
Psalms 37:18.content: God, who knows His people's changes, provides against evil and supplies all their need.

Psalms 37:19.title: Psalms 37:18-19
Psalms 37:19.content: God, who knows His people's changes, provides against evil and supplies all their need.

Psalms 37:20.title: Psalms 37:20
Psalms 37:20.content: While the wicked, however mighty, are destroyed, and that utterly, as smoke which vanishes and leaves no trace.

Psalms 37:21.title: Psalms 37:21-22
Psalms 37:21.content: payeth not—not able; having grown poor (compare De 15:7). Ability of the one and inability of the other do not exclude moral dispositions. God's blessing or cursing makes the difference.

Psalms 37:22.title: Psalms 37:21-22
Psalms 37:22.content: payeth not—not able; having grown poor (compare De 15:7). Ability of the one and inability of the other do not exclude moral dispositions. God's blessing or cursing makes the difference.

Psalms 37:22.title: Psalms 37:22
Psalms 37:22.content: cut off—opposed to "inherit the earth" (compare Le 7:20, 21).

Psalms 37:23.title: Psalms 37:23-24
Psalms 37:23.content: steps—way, or, "course of life"; as ordered by God, failures will not be permanent.

Psalms 37:24.title: Psalms 37:23-24
Psalms 37:24.content: steps—way, or, "course of life"; as ordered by God, failures will not be permanent.

Psalms 37:26.title: Psalms 37:26
Psalms 37:26.content: his seed is blessed—literally, "for a blessing" (Ge 12:2; Ps 21:6). This position is still true as the rule of God's economy (1Ti 4:8; 6:6).

Psalms 37:27.title: Psalms 37:27-29
Psalms 37:27.content: The exhortation is sustained by the assurance of God's essential rectitude in that providential government which provides perpetual blessings for the good, and perpetual misery for the wicked.

Psalms 37:28.title: Psalms 37:27-29
Psalms 37:28.content: The exhortation is sustained by the assurance of God's essential rectitude in that providential government which provides perpetual blessings for the good, and perpetual misery for the wicked.

Psalms 37:29.title: Psalms 37:27-29
Psalms 37:29.content: The exhortation is sustained by the assurance of God's essential rectitude in that providential government which provides perpetual blessings for the good, and perpetual misery for the wicked.

Psalms 37:30.title: Psalms 37:30-31
Psalms 37:30.content: The righteous described as to the elements of character, thought, word, and action.

Psalms 37:31.title: Psalms 37:30-31
Psalms 37:31.content: The righteous described as to the elements of character, thought, word, and action.

Psalms 37:32.title: Psalms 37:32-33
Psalms 37:32.content: The devices of the wicked against the good fail because God acquits them.

Psalms 37:33.title: Psalms 37:32-33
Psalms 37:33.content: The devices of the wicked against the good fail because God acquits them.

Psalms 37:34.title: Psalms 37:34
Psalms 37:34.content: On the contrary, the good are not only blessed, but made to see the ruin of their foes.

Psalms 37:35.title: Psalms 37:35-36
Psalms 37:35.content: of which a picture is given, under the figure of a flourishing tree (compare Margin), which soon withers.

Psalms 37:36.title: Psalms 37:35-36
Psalms 37:36.content: of which a picture is given, under the figure of a flourishing tree (compare Margin), which soon withers.

Psalms 37:37.title: Psalms 37:37
Psalms 37:37.content: By "the end" is meant reward (Pr 23:18; 24:14), or expectation of success, as in Ps 37:38, which describes the end of the wicked in contrast, and that is cut off (compare Ps 73:17).

Psalms 37:39.title: Psalms 37:39-40
Psalms 37:39.content: strength—(Ps 27:1; 28:8). trouble—straits (Ps 9:9; 10:1). In trust and quietness is the salvation of the pious from all foes and all their devices.

Psalms 37:40.title: Psalms 37:39-40
Psalms 37:40.content: strength—(Ps 27:1; 28:8). trouble—straits (Ps 9:9; 10:1). In trust and quietness is the salvation of the pious from all foes and all their devices.

Psalms 38:1.title: Psalms 38:1-4
Psalms 38:1.content: He deprecates deserved punishment, which is described (Ps 6:1), under the figure of bodily disease [Ps 38:3].

Psalms 38:2.title: Psalms 38:1-4
Psalms 38:2.content: He deprecates deserved punishment, which is described (Ps 6:1), under the figure of bodily disease [Ps 38:3].

Psalms 38:2.title: Psalms 38:2
Psalms 38:2.content: arrows … and thy hand—the sharp and heavy afflictions he suffered (De 32:23).

Psalms 38:3.title: Psalms 38:1-4
Psalms 38:3.content: He deprecates deserved punishment, which is described (Ps 6:1), under the figure of bodily disease [Ps 38:3].

Psalms 38:4.title: Psalms 38:1-4
Psalms 38:4.content: He deprecates deserved punishment, which is described (Ps 6:1), under the figure of bodily disease [Ps 38:3].

Psalms 38:4.title: Psalms 38:4
Psalms 38:4.content: iniquities—afflictions in punishment of sin (2Sa 16:12; Ps 31:10; 40:12). gone over mine head—as a flood.

Psalms 38:5.title: Psalms 38:5-8
Psalms 38:5.content: The loathsomeness, corruption, and wasting torture of severe physical disease set forth his mental anguish [Ps 38:6]. It is possible some bodily disease was connected. The loins are the seat of strength. His exhaustion left him only the power to groan [Ps 38:9].

Psalms 38:6.title: Psalms 38:5-8
Psalms 38:6.content: The loathsomeness, corruption, and wasting torture of severe physical disease set forth his mental anguish [Ps 38:6]. It is possible some bodily disease was connected. The loins are the seat of strength. His exhaustion left him only the power to groan [Ps 38:9].

Psalms 38:7.title: Psalms 38:5-8
Psalms 38:7.content: The loathsomeness, corruption, and wasting torture of severe physical disease set forth his mental anguish [Ps 38:6]. It is possible some bodily disease was connected. The loins are the seat of strength. His exhaustion left him only the power to groan [Ps 38:9].

Psalms 38:8.title: Psalms 38:5-8
Psalms 38:8.content: The loathsomeness, corruption, and wasting torture of severe physical disease set forth his mental anguish [Ps 38:6]. It is possible some bodily disease was connected. The loins are the seat of strength. His exhaustion left him only the power to groan [Ps 38:9].

Psalms 38:10.title: Psalms 38:10
Psalms 38:10.content: My heart panteth—as if barely surviving. light … from me—utter exhaustion (Ps 6:7; 13:3).

Psalms 38:11.title: Psalms 38:11-12
Psalms 38:11.content: Friends desert, but foes increase in malignity.

Psalms 38:12.title: Psalms 38:11-12
Psalms 38:12.content: Friends desert, but foes increase in malignity.

Psalms 38:13.title: Psalms 38:13-14
Psalms 38:13.content: He patiently submits, uttering no reproaches or replies (Joh 19:9) to their insulting speeches;

Psalms 38:14.title: Psalms 38:13-14
Psalms 38:14.content: He patiently submits, uttering no reproaches or replies (Joh 19:9) to their insulting speeches;

Psalms 38:15.title: Psalms 38:15-17
Psalms 38:15.content: for he is confident the Lord—literally, "Sovereign" (to whom he was a servant), would answer his prayer (Ps 3:4; 4:1), and not permit their triumph in his partial halting, of which he was in danger.

Psalms 38:16.title: Psalms 38:15-17
Psalms 38:16.content: for he is confident the Lord—literally, "Sovereign" (to whom he was a servant), would answer his prayer (Ps 3:4; 4:1), and not permit their triumph in his partial halting, of which he was in danger.

Psalms 38:17.title: Psalms 38:15-17
Psalms 38:17.content: for he is confident the Lord—literally, "Sovereign" (to whom he was a servant), would answer his prayer (Ps 3:4; 4:1), and not permit their triumph in his partial halting, of which he was in danger.

Psalms 38:18.title: Psalms 38:18
Psalms 38:18.content: Consciousness of sin makes suffering pungent, and suffering, rightly received, leads to confession.

Psalms 38:19.title: Psalms 38:19-20
Psalms 38:19.content: Still, while humbled before God, he is the victim of deadly enemies, full of malice and treachery. enemies are lively—literally, "of life," who would take my life, that is, deadly.

Psalms 38:20.title: Psalms 38:19-20
Psalms 38:20.content: Still, while humbled before God, he is the victim of deadly enemies, full of malice and treachery. enemies are lively—literally, "of life," who would take my life, that is, deadly.

Psalms 38:21.title: Psalms 38:21-22
Psalms 38:21.content: (Compare Ps 22:19; 35:3). All terms of frequent use. In this Psalm the language is generally susceptible of application to Christ as a sufferer, David, as such, typifying Him. This does not require us to apply the confessions of sin, but only the pains or penalties which He bore for us.

Psalms 38:22.title: Psalms 38:21-22
Psalms 38:22.content: (Compare Ps 22:19; 35:3). All terms of frequent use. In this Psalm the language is generally susceptible of application to Christ as a sufferer, David, as such, typifying Him. This does not require us to apply the confessions of sin, but only the pains or penalties which He bore for us.

Psalms 39:1.title: Psalms 39:1
Psalms 39:1.content: I said—or, "resolved." will take heed—watch. ways—conduct, of which the use of the tongue is a part (Jas 1:26). bridle—literally, "muzzle for my mouth" (compare De 25:4). while … before me—in beholding their prosperity (Ps 37:10, 36).

Psalms 39:3.title: Psalms 39:3
Psalms 39:3.content: His emotions, as a smothered flame, burst forth.

Psalms 39:4.title: Psalms 39:4-7
Psalms 39:4.content: Some take these words as those of fretting, but they are not essentially such. The tinge of discontent arises from the character of his suppressed emotions. But, addressing God, they are softened and subdued. make me to know mine end—experimentally appreciate. how frail I am—literally, "when I shall cease."

Psalms 39:5.title: Psalms 39:4-7
Psalms 39:5.content: Some take these words as those of fretting, but they are not essentially such. The tinge of discontent arises from the character of his suppressed emotions. But, addressing God, they are softened and subdued. make me to know mine end—experimentally appreciate. how frail I am—literally, "when I shall cease."

Psalms 39:5.title: Psalms 39:5-6
Psalms 39:5.content: His prayer is answered in his obtaining an impressive view of the vanity of the life of all men, and their transient state. Their pomp is a mere image, and their wealth is gathered they know not for whom.

Psalms 39:6.title: Psalms 39:4-7
Psalms 39:6.content: Some take these words as those of fretting, but they are not essentially such. The tinge of discontent arises from the character of his suppressed emotions. But, addressing God, they are softened and subdued. make me to know mine end—experimentally appreciate. how frail I am—literally, "when I shall cease."

Psalms 39:6.content: His prayer is answered in his obtaining an impressive view of the vanity of the life of all men, and their transient state. Their pomp is a mere image, and their wealth is gathered they know not for whom.
