Psalms 39:7.content: Some take these words as those of fretting, but they are not essentially such. The tinge of discontent arises from the character of his suppressed emotions. But, addressing God, they are softened and subdued. make me to know mine end—experimentally appreciate. how frail I am—literally, "when I shall cease."

Psalms 39:7.title: Psalms 39:7
Psalms 39:7.content: The interrogation makes the implied negative stronger. Though this world offers nothing to our expectation, God is worthy of all confidence.

Psalms 39:8.title: Psalms 39:8-10
Psalms 39:8.content: Patiently submissive, he prays for the removal of his chastisement, and that he may not be a reproach.

Psalms 39:9.title: Psalms 39:8-10
Psalms 39:9.content: Patiently submissive, he prays for the removal of his chastisement, and that he may not be a reproach.

Psalms 39:10.title: Psalms 39:8-10
Psalms 39:10.content: Patiently submissive, he prays for the removal of his chastisement, and that he may not be a reproach.

Psalms 39:11.title: Psalms 39:11
Psalms 39:11.content: From his own case, he argues to that of all, that the destruction of man's enjoyments is ascribable to sin.

Psalms 39:12.title: Psalms 39:12-13
Psalms 39:12.content: Consonant with the tenor of the Psalm, he prays for God's compassionate regard to him as a stranger here; and that, as such was the condition of his fathers, so, like them, he may be cheered instead of being bound under wrath and chastened in displeasure.

Psalms 39:13.title: Psalms 39:12-13
Psalms 39:13.content: Consonant with the tenor of the Psalm, he prays for God's compassionate regard to him as a stranger here; and that, as such was the condition of his fathers, so, like them, he may be cheered instead of being bound under wrath and chastened in displeasure.

Psalms 40:1.title: Psalms 40:1-3
Psalms 40:1.content: The figures for deep distress are illustrated in Jeremiah's history (Jer 38:6-12). Patience and trust manifested in distress, deliverance in answer to prayer, and the blessed effect of it in eliciting praise from God's true worshippers, teach us that Christ's suffering is our example, and His deliverance our encouragement (Heb 5:7, 8; 12:3; 1Pe 4:12-16). inclined—(the ear, Ps 17:6), as if to catch the faintest sigh.

Psalms 40:2.title: Psalms 40:1-3
Psalms 40:2.content: The figures for deep distress are illustrated in Jeremiah's history (Jer 38:6-12). Patience and trust manifested in distress, deliverance in answer to prayer, and the blessed effect of it in eliciting praise from God's true worshippers, teach us that Christ's suffering is our example, and His deliverance our encouragement (Heb 5:7, 8; 12:3; 1Pe 4:12-16). inclined—(the ear, Ps 17:6), as if to catch the faintest sigh.

Psalms 40:3.title: Psalms 40:1-3
Psalms 40:3.content: The figures for deep distress are illustrated in Jeremiah's history (Jer 38:6-12). Patience and trust manifested in distress, deliverance in answer to prayer, and the blessed effect of it in eliciting praise from God's true worshippers, teach us that Christ's suffering is our example, and His deliverance our encouragement (Heb 5:7, 8; 12:3; 1Pe 4:12-16). inclined—(the ear, Ps 17:6), as if to catch the faintest sigh.

Psalms 40:3.title: Psalms 40:3
Psalms 40:3.content: a new song—(See on Ps 33:3). fear, and … trust—revere with love and faith.

Psalms 40:4.title: Psalms 40:4
Psalms 40:4.content: Blessed—(Ps 1:1; 2:12). respecteth—literally, "turns towards," as an object of confidence. turn aside—from true God and His law to falsehood in worship and conduct.

Psalms 40:5.title: Psalms 40:5
Psalms 40:5.content: be reckoned up in order—(compare Ps 5:3; 33:14; Isa 44:7), too many to be set forth regularly. This is but one instance of many. The use of the plural accords with the union of Christ and His people. In suffering and triumph, they are one with Him.

Psalms 40:6.title: Psalms 40:6-8
Psalms 40:6.content: In Paul's view this passage has more meaning than the mere expression of grateful devotion to God's service. He represents Christ as declaring that the sacrifices, whether vegetable or animal, general or special expiatory offerings, would not avail to meet the demands of God's law, and that He had come to render the required satisfaction, which he states was effected by "the offering of the body of Christ" [Heb 10:10], for that is the "will of God" which Christ came to fulfil or do, in order to effect man's redemption. We thus see that the contrast to the unsatisfactory character assigned the Old Testament offerings in Ps 40:6 is found in the compliance with God's law (compare Ps 40:7, 8). Of course, as Paul and other New Testament writers explain Christ's work, it consisted in more than being made under the law or obeying its precepts. It required an "obedience unto death" [Php 2:8], and that is the compliance here chiefly intended, and which makes the contrast with Ps 40:6 clear. mine ears hast thou opened—Whether allusion is made to the custom of boring a servant's ear, in token of voluntary and perpetual enslavement (Ex 21:6), or that the opening of the ear, as in Isa 48:8; 50:5 (though by a different word in Hebrew) denotes obedience by the common figure of hearing for obeying, it is evident that the clause is designed to express a devotion to God's will as avowed more fully in Ps 40:8, and already explained. Paul, however, uses the words, "a body hast thou prepared me" [Heb 10:5], which are found in the Septuagint in the place of the words, "mine ears hast thou opened." He does not lay any stress on this clause, and his argument is complete without it. It is, perhaps, to be regarded rather as an interpretation or free translation by the Septuagint, than either an addition or attempt at verbal translation. The Septuagint translators may have had reference to Christ's vicarious sufferings as taught in other Scriptures, as in Isa 53:4-11; at all events, the sense is substantially the same, as a body was essential to the required obedience (compare Ro 7:4; 1Pe 2:24).

Psalms 40:7.title: Psalms 40:7
Psalms 40:7.content: Then—in such case, without necessarily referring to order of time. Lo, I come—I am prepared to do, &c. in the volume of the book—roll of the book. Such rolls, resembling maps, are still used in the synagogues. written of me—or on me, prescribed to me (2Ki 22:13). The first is the sense adopted by Paul. In either case, the Pentateuch, or law of Moses, is meant, and while it contains much respecting Christ directly, as Ge 3:15; 49:10; De 18:15, and, indirectly, in the Levitical ritual, there is nowhere any allusion to David.

Psalms 40:9.title: Psalms 40:9-10
Psalms 40:9.content: I have preached—literally, "announced good tidings." Christ's prophetical office is taught. He "preached" the great truths of God's government of sinners.

Psalms 40:10.title: Psalms 40:9-10
Psalms 40:10.content: I have preached—literally, "announced good tidings." Christ's prophetical office is taught. He "preached" the great truths of God's government of sinners.

Psalms 40:11.title: Psalms 40:11
Psalms 40:11.content: may be rendered as an assertion, that God will not withhold (Ps 16:1).

Psalms 40:12.title: Psalms 40:12
Psalms 40:12.content: evils—inflicted by others. iniquities—or penal afflictions, and sometimes calamities in the wide sense. This meaning of the word is very common (Ps 31:11; 38:4; compare Ge 4:13, Cain's punishment; Ge 19:15, that of Sodom; 1Sa 28:10, of the witch of En-dor; also 2Sa 16:12; Job 19:29; Isa 5:18; 53:11). This meaning of the word is also favored by the clause, "taken hold of me," which follows, which can be said appropriately of sufferings, but not of sins (compare Job 27:20; Ps 69:24). Thus, the difficulties in referring this Psalm to Christ, arising from the usual reading of this verse, are removed. Of the terrible afflictions, or sufferings, alluded to and endured for us, compare Lu 22:39-44, and the narrative of the scenes of Calvary. my heart faileth me—(Mt 26:38), "My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death." cannot look up—literally, "I cannot see," not denoting the depression of conscious guilt, as Lu 18:13, but exhaustion from suffering, as dimness of eyes (compare Ps 6:7; 13:3; 38:10). The whole context thus sustains the sense assigned to iniquities.

Psalms 40:14.title: Psalms 40:14-15
Psalms 40:14.content: The language is not necessarily imprecatory, but rather a confident expectation (Ps 5:11), though the former sense is not inconsistent with Christ's prayer for the forgiveness of His murderers, inasmuch as their confusion and shame might be the very means to prepare them for humbly seeking forgiveness (compare Ac 2:37).

Psalms 40:15.title: Psalms 40:14-15
Psalms 40:15.content: The language is not necessarily imprecatory, but rather a confident expectation (Ps 5:11), though the former sense is not inconsistent with Christ's prayer for the forgiveness of His murderers, inasmuch as their confusion and shame might be the very means to prepare them for humbly seeking forgiveness (compare Ac 2:37).

Psalms 40:15.title: Psalms 40:15
Psalms 40:15.content: for a reward—literally, "in consequence of." Aha—(Compare Ps 35:21, 25).

Psalms 40:16.title: Psalms 40:16
Psalms 40:16.content: (Compare Ps 35:27). love thy salvation—delight in its bestowal on others as well as themselves.

Psalms 40:17.title: Psalms 40:17
Psalms 40:17.content: A summary of his condition and hopes. thinketh upon—or provides for me. "He was heard," "when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears, unto Him that was able to save him from death" [Heb 5:7].

Psalms 41:1.title: Psalms 41:1-3
Psalms 41:1.content: God rewards kindness to the poor (Pr 19:17). From Ps 41:2, 11 it may be inferred that the Psalmist describes his own conduct. poor—in person, position, and possessions.

Psalms 41:2.title: Psalms 41:1-3
Psalms 41:2.content: God rewards kindness to the poor (Pr 19:17). From Ps 41:2, 11 it may be inferred that the Psalmist describes his own conduct. poor—in person, position, and possessions.

Psalms 41:2.title: Psalms 41:2
Psalms 41:2.content: shall be blessed—literally, "led aright," or "safely," prospered (Ps 23:3). upon the earth—or land of promise (Ps 25:13; 27:3-9, &c.).

Psalms 41:3.title: Psalms 41:1-3
Psalms 41:3.content: God rewards kindness to the poor (Pr 19:17). From Ps 41:2, 11 it may be inferred that the Psalmist describes his own conduct. poor—in person, position, and possessions.

Psalms 41:3.title: Psalms 41:3
Psalms 41:3.content: The figures of Ps 41:3 are drawn from the acts of a kind nurse.

Psalms 41:4.title: Psalms 41:4
Psalms 41:4.content: I said—I asked the mercy I show. heal my soul—(Compare Ps 30:2). "Sin and suffering are united," is one of the great teachings of the Psalms.

Psalms 41:5.title: Psalms 41:5-6
Psalms 41:5.content: A graphic picture of the conduct of a malignant enemy.

Psalms 41:6.title: Psalms 41:5-6
Psalms 41:6.content: A graphic picture of the conduct of a malignant enemy.

Psalms 41:6.title: Psalms 41:6
Psalms 41:6.content: to see me—as if to spy out my case. he speaketh … itself—or, "he speaketh vanity as to his heart"—that is, does not speak candidly, "he gathereth iniquity to him," collects elements for mischief, and then divulges the gains of his hypocrisy.

Psalms 41:7.title: Psalms 41:7-8
Psalms 41:7.content: So of others, all act alike.

Psalms 41:8.title: Psalms 41:7-8
Psalms 41:8.content: So of others, all act alike.

Psalms 41:8.title: Psalms 41:8
Psalms 41:8.content: An evil disease—literally, "a word of Belial," some slander. cleaveth—literally, "poured on him." that he lieth—who has now laid down, "he is utterly undone and our victory is sure."

Psalms 41:9.title: Psalms 41:9
Psalms 41:9.content: mine … friend—literally, "the man of my peace." eat … bread—who depended on me or was well treated by me. hath lifted up heel—in scornful violence. As David and his fortunes typified Christ and His (compare Introduction), so these words expressed the treatment he received, and also that of his Son and Lord; hence, though not distinctly prophetical, our Saviour (Joh 13:18) applies them to Judas, "that the Scripture may be fulfilled." This last phrase has a wide use in the New Testament, and is not restricted to denote special prophecies.

Psalms 41:10.title: Psalms 41:10
Psalms 41:10.content: A lawful punishment of criminals is not revenge, nor inconsistent with their final good (compare Ps 40:14, 15).

Psalms 41:11.title: Psalms 41:11-13
Psalms 41:11.content: favourest—or tenderly lovest me (Ge 34:19), evinced by relief from his enemies, and, farther, God recognizes his innocence by upholding him.

Psalms 41:12.title: Psalms 41:11-13
Psalms 41:12.content: favourest—or tenderly lovest me (Ge 34:19), evinced by relief from his enemies, and, farther, God recognizes his innocence by upholding him.

Psalms 41:12.title: Psalms 41:12
Psalms 41:12.content: settest … before thy face—under thy watch and care, as God before man's face (Ps 16:8) is an object of trust and love.

Psalms 41:13.title: Psalms 41:11-13
Psalms 41:13.content: favourest—or tenderly lovest me (Ge 34:19), evinced by relief from his enemies, and, farther, God recognizes his innocence by upholding him.

Psalms 41:13.title: Psalms 41:13
Psalms 41:13.content: Blessed—praised, usually applied to God. The word usually applied to men denotes happiness (Ps 1:1; 32:1). With this doxology the first book closes.

Psalms 42:1.title: Psalms 42:1-2
Psalms 42:1.content: Compare (Ps 63:1). panteth—desires in a state of exhaustion.

Psalms 42:2.title: Psalms 42:1-2
Psalms 42:2.content: Compare (Ps 63:1). panteth—desires in a state of exhaustion.

Psalms 42:2.title: Psalms 42:2
Psalms 42:2.content: appear before God—in acts of worship, the terms used in the command for the stated personal appearance of the Jews at the sanctuary.

Psalms 42:3.title: Psalms 42:3
Psalms 42:3.content: Where is thy God?—implying that He had forsaken him (compare 2Sa 16:7; Ps 3:2; 22:8).

Psalms 42:4.title: Psalms 42:4
Psalms 42:4.content: The verbs are properly rendered as futures, "I will remember," &c.,—that is, the recollection of this season of distress will give greater zest to the privileges of God's worship, when obtained.

Psalms 42:5.title: Psalms 42:5
Psalms 42:5.content: Hence he chides his despondent soul, assuring himself of a time of joy. help of his countenance—or, "face" (compare Nu 6:25; Ps 4:6; 16:11).

Psalms 42:6.title: Psalms 42:6
Psalms 42:6.content: Dejection again described. therefore—that is, finding no comfort in myself, I turn to Thee, even in this distant "land of Jordan and the (mountains) Hermon, the country east of Jordan. hill Mizar—as a name of a small hill contrasted with the mountains round about Jerusalem, perhaps denoted the contempt with which the place of exile was regarded.

Psalms 42:7.title: Psalms 42:7
Psalms 42:7.content: The roar of successive billows, responding to that of floods of rain, represented the heavy waves of sorrow which overwhelmed him.

Psalms 42:8.title: Psalms 42:8
Psalms 42:8.content: Still he relies on as constant a flow of divine mercy which will elicit his praise and encourage his prayer to God.

Psalms 42:9.title: Psalms 42:9-10
Psalms 42:9.content: in view of which [Ps 42:8], he dictates to himself a prayer based on his distress, aggravated as it was by the cruel taunts and infidel suggestions of his foes.

Psalms 42:10.title: Psalms 42:9-10
Psalms 42:10.content: in view of which [Ps 42:8], he dictates to himself a prayer based on his distress, aggravated as it was by the cruel taunts and infidel suggestions of his foes.

Psalms 42:11.title: Psalms 42:11
Psalms 42:11.content: This brings on a renewed self-chiding, and excites hopes of relief. health—or help. of my countenance—(compare Ps 42:5) who cheers me, driving away clouds of sorrow from my face. my God—It is He of whose existence and favor my foes would have me doubt.

Psalms 43:1.title: Psalms 43:1
Psalms 43:1.content: Judge—or, "vindicate" (Ps 10:18). plead, &c.—(Ps 35:1). ungodly—neither in character or condition objects of God's favor (compare Ps 4:3).

Psalms 43:2.title: Psalms 43:2
Psalms 43:2.content: God of my strength—by covenant relation my stronghold (Ps 18:1). cast me off—in scorn. because—or, "in," that is, in such circumstances of oppression.

Psalms 43:3.title: Psalms 43:3
Psalms 43:3.content: light—as in Ps 27:1. truth—or, "faithfulness" (Ps 25:5), manifest it by fulfilling promises. Light and truth are personified as messengers who will bring him to the privileged place of worship. tabernacles—plural, in allusion to the various courts.

Psalms 43:4.title: Psalms 43:4
Psalms 43:4.content: the altar—as the chief place of worship. The mention of the harp suggests the prominence of praise in his offering.

Psalms 44:1.title: Psalms 44:1-3
Psalms 44:1.content: This period is that of the settlement of Canaan (Jos 24:12; Jud 6:3). have told—or, "related" (compare Ex 10:2).

Psalms 44:2.title: Psalms 44:1-3
Psalms 44:2.content: This period is that of the settlement of Canaan (Jos 24:12; Jud 6:3). have told—or, "related" (compare Ex 10:2).

Psalms 44:2.title: Psalms 44:2
Psalms 44:2.content: plantedst them—that is, "our fathers," who are also, from the parallel construction of the last clause, to be regarded as the object of "cast them out," which means—literally, "send" them out, or, "extend them." Heathen and people denote the nations who were driven out to make room for the Israelites.

Psalms 44:3.title: Psalms 44:1-3
Psalms 44:3.content: This period is that of the settlement of Canaan (Jos 24:12; Jud 6:3). have told—or, "related" (compare Ex 10:2).

Psalms 44:4.title: Psalms 44:4
Psalms 44:4.content: Thou art my King—literally, "he who is my King," sustaining the same covenant relation as to the "fathers."

Psalms 44:5.title: Psalms 44:5
Psalms 44:5.content: The figure drawn from the habits of the ox.

Psalms 44:6.title: Psalms 44:6-8
Psalms 44:6.content: God is not only our sole help, but only worthy of praise.

Psalms 44:7.title: Psalms 44:6-8
Psalms 44:7.content: God is not only our sole help, but only worthy of praise.

Psalms 44:8.title: Psalms 44:6-8
Psalms 44:8.content: God is not only our sole help, but only worthy of praise.

Psalms 44:9.title: Psalms 44:9
Psalms 44:9.content: But—contrasting, cast off as abhorrent (Ps 43:2). goest not forth—literally, "will not go" (2Sa 5:23). In several consecutive verses the leading verb is future, and the following one past (in Hebrew), thus denoting the causes and effects. Thus (Ps 44:10-12), when defeated, spoiling follows; when delivered as sheep, dispersion follows, &c.

Psalms 44:11.title: Psalms 44:11
Psalms 44:11.content: The Babylonian captivity not necessarily meant. There were others (compare 1Ki 8:46).

Psalms 44:16.title: Psalms 44:16
Psalms 44:16.content: Its cause, the taunts and presence of malignant enemies (Ps 8:2).

Psalms 44:17.title: Psalms 44:17-19
Psalms 44:17.content: They had not apostatized totally—were still God's people.

Psalms 44:18.title: Psalms 44:17-19
Psalms 44:18.content: They had not apostatized totally—were still God's people.

Psalms 44:19.title: Psalms 44:17-19
Psalms 44:19.content: They had not apostatized totally—were still God's people.

Psalms 44:19.title: Psalms 44:19
Psalms 44:19.content: sore broken—crushed. place of dragons—desolate, barren, rocky wilderness (Ps 63:10; Isa 13:22), shadow of death—(Compare Ps 23:4).

Psalms 44:20.title: Psalms 44:20-21
Psalms 44:20.content: A solemn appeal to God to witness their constancy. stretched out … hands—gesture of worship (Ex 9:29; Ps 88:9).

Psalms 44:21.title: Psalms 44:20-21
Psalms 44:21.content: A solemn appeal to God to witness their constancy. stretched out … hands—gesture of worship (Ex 9:29; Ps 88:9).

Psalms 44:22.title: Psalms 44:22
Psalms 44:22.content: Their protracted sufferings as God's people attests the constancy. Paul (Ro 8:36) uses this to describe Christian steadfastness in persecution.

Psalms 44:23.title: Psalms 44:23-26
Psalms 44:23.content: This style of addressing God, as indifferent, is frequent (Ps 3:7; 9:19; 13:1, &c.). However low their condition, God is appealed to, on the ground, and for the honor, of His mercy.

Psalms 44:24.title: Psalms 44:23-26
Psalms 44:24.content: This style of addressing God, as indifferent, is frequent (Ps 3:7; 9:19; 13:1, &c.). However low their condition, God is appealed to, on the ground, and for the honor, of His mercy.

Psalms 44:25.title: Psalms 44:23-26
Psalms 44:25.content: This style of addressing God, as indifferent, is frequent (Ps 3:7; 9:19; 13:1, &c.). However low their condition, God is appealed to, on the ground, and for the honor, of His mercy.

Psalms 44:26.title: Psalms 44:23-26
Psalms 44:26.content: This style of addressing God, as indifferent, is frequent (Ps 3:7; 9:19; 13:1, &c.). However low their condition, God is appealed to, on the ground, and for the honor, of His mercy.

Psalms 45:1.title: Psalms 45:1
Psalms 45:1.content: An animated preface indicative of strong emotion. Literally, "My heart overflows: a good matter I speak; the things which I have made," &c. inditing—literally, "boiling up," as a fountain overflows. my tongue is the pen—a mere instrument of God's use. of a ready writer—that is, it is fluent. The theme is inspiring and language flows fast.

Psalms 45:2.title: Psalms 45:2
Psalms 45:2.content: To rich personal attractions is added grace of the lips, captivating powers of speech. This is given, and becomes a source of power and proves a blessing. Christ is a prophet (Lu 4:22).

Psalms 45:3.title: Psalms 45:3-4
Psalms 45:3.content: The king is addressed as ready to go forth to battle. sword—(Compare Re 1:16; 19:15). mighty—(Compare Isa 9:6). glory and … majesty—generally used as divine attributes (Ps 96:6; 104:1; 111:3), or as specially conferred on mortals (Ps 21:5), perhaps these typically.

Psalms 45:4.title: Psalms 45:3-4
Psalms 45:4.content: The king is addressed as ready to go forth to battle. sword—(Compare Re 1:16; 19:15). mighty—(Compare Isa 9:6). glory and … majesty—generally used as divine attributes (Ps 96:6; 104:1; 111:3), or as specially conferred on mortals (Ps 21:5), perhaps these typically.

Psalms 45:4.title: Psalms 45:4
Psalms 45:4.content: ride prosperously—or conduct a successful war. because of—for the interests of truth, &c. meekness … righteousness—without any connection—that is, a righteousness or equity of government, distinguished by meekness or condescension (Ps 18:35). right hand—or power, as its organ. shall teach thee—point the way to terrible things; that is, in conquest of enemies.

Psalms 45:5.title: Psalms 45:5
Psalms 45:5.content: The result. people—Whole nations are subdued.

Psalms 45:6.title: Psalms 45:6
Psalms 45:6.content: No lawful construction can be devised to change the sense here given and sustained by the ancient versions, and above all by Paul (Heb 1:8). Of the perpetuity of this government, compare 2Sa 7:13; Ps 10:16; 72:5; 89:4; 110:4; Isa 9:7.

Psalms 45:7.title: Psalms 45:7
Psalms 45:7.content: As in Ps 45:6 the divine nature is made prominent, here the moral qualities of the human are alleged as the reason or ground of the mediatorial exultation. Some render "O God, thy God," instead of God, thy God—but the latter is sustained by the same form (Ps 50:7), and it was only of His human nature that the anointing could be predicated (compare Isa 61:3). oil of gladness—or token of gladness, as used in feasts and other times of solemn joy (compare 1Ki 1:39, 40). fellows—other kings.

Psalms 45:8.title: Psalms 45:8
Psalms 45:8.content: The king thus inaugurated is now presented as a bridegroom, who appears in garments richly perfumed, brought out from ivory palaces—His royal residence; by which, as indications of the happy bridal occasion, He has been gladdened.

Psalms 45:9.title: Psalms 45:9
Psalms 45:9.content: In completion of this picture of a marriage festival, female attendants or bridesmaids of the highest rank attend Him, while the queen, in rich apparel (Ps 45:13), stands ready for the nuptial procession.

Psalms 45:10.title: Psalms 45:10-11
Psalms 45:10.content: She is invited to the union, for forming which she must leave her father's people. She representing, by the form of the allegory, the Church, this address is illustrated by all those scriptures, from Ge 12:1 on, which speak of the people of God as a chosen, separate, and peculiar people. The relation of subjection to her spouse at once accords with the law of marriage, as given in Ge 3:16; 18:12; Eph 5:22; 1Pe 3:5, 6, and the relation of the Church to Christ (Eph 5:24). The love of the husband is intimately connected with the entire devotion to which the bride is exhorted.

Psalms 45:11.title: Psalms 45:10-11
Psalms 45:11.content: She is invited to the union, for forming which she must leave her father's people. She representing, by the form of the allegory, the Church, this address is illustrated by all those scriptures, from Ge 12:1 on, which speak of the people of God as a chosen, separate, and peculiar people. The relation of subjection to her spouse at once accords with the law of marriage, as given in Ge 3:16; 18:12; Eph 5:22; 1Pe 3:5, 6, and the relation of the Church to Christ (Eph 5:24). The love of the husband is intimately connected with the entire devotion to which the bride is exhorted.

Psalms 45:12.title: Psalms 45:12
Psalms 45:12.content: daughter of Tyre—(Ps 9:14); denotes the people. Tyre, celebrated for its great wealth, is selected to represent the richest nations, an idea confirmed by the next clause. These gifts are brought as means to conciliate the royal parties, representing the admitted subjection of the offerers. This well sets forth the exalted position of the Church and her head, whose moral qualities receive the homage of the world. The contribution of material wealth to sustain the institutions of the Church may be included (compare "riches of the Gentiles," Ps 72:10; Isa 60:5-10).

Psalms 45:13.title: Psalms 45:13
Psalms 45:13.content: the king's daughter—a term of dignity. It may also intimate, with some allusion to the teaching of the allegory, that the bride of Christ, the Church, is the daughter of the great king, God. within—Not only is her outward raiment costly, but all her apparel is of the richest texture. wrought gold—gold embroidery, or cloth in which gold is woven.

Psalms 45:14.title: Psalms 45:14-15
Psalms 45:14.content: The progress of the procession is described; according to the usual custom the bride and attendants are conducted to the palace. Some for the words— in raiment of needlework—propose another rendering, "on variegated (or embroidered) cloths"—that is, in the manner of the East, richly wrought tapestry was spread on the ground, on which the bride walked. As the dress had been already mentioned, this seems to be a probable translation.

Psalms 45:15.title: Psalms 45:14-15
Psalms 45:15.content: The progress of the procession is described; according to the usual custom the bride and attendants are conducted to the palace. Psalms 45:15.title: Psalms 45:15
Psalms 45:15.content: shall they be brought—in solemn form (compare Job 10:19; 21:22). The entrance into the palace with great joy closes the scene. So shall the Church be finally brought to her Lord, and united amid the festivities of the holy beings in heaven.

Psalms 45:16.title: Psalms 45:16
Psalms 45:16.content: As earthly monarchs govern widely extended empires by viceroys, this glorious king is represented as supplying all the principalities of earth with princes of his own numerous progeny.

Psalms 45:17.title: Psalms 45:17
Psalms 45:17.content: The glories of this empire shall be as wide as the world and lasting as eternity. therefore—Because thus glorious, the praise shall be universal and perpetual. Some writers have taxed their ingenuity to find in the history and fortunes of Christ and His Church exact parallels for every part of this splendid allegory, not excepting its gorgeous Oriental imagery. Thus, by the dresses of the king and queen, are thought to be meant the eminent endowments and graces of Christ and His people. The attendant women, supposed (though inconsistently it might seem with the inspired character of the work) to be concubines, are thought to represent the Gentile churches, and the bride the Jewish, &c. But it is evident that we cannot pursue such a mode of interpretation. For, following the allegory, we must suspend to the distant future the results of a union whose consummation as a marriage is still distant (compare Re 21:9). In fact, the imagery here and elsewhere sets before us the Church in two aspects. As a body, it is yet incomplete, the whole is yet ungathered. As a moral institution, it is yet imperfect. In the final catastrophe it will be complete and perfect. Thus, as a bride adorned, &c., it will be united with its Lord. Thus the union of Christ and the Church triumphant is set forth. On the other hand, in regard to its component parts, the relation of Christ as head, as husband, &c., already exists, and as these parts form an institution in this world, it is by His union with it, and the gifts and graces with which He endows it, that a spiritual seed arises and spreads in the world. Hence we must fix our minds only on the one simple but grand truth, that Christ loves the Church, is head over all things for it, raises it in His exaltation to the highest moral dignity—a dignity of which every, even the meanest, sincere disciple will partake. As to the time, then, in which this allegorical prophecy is to fulfilled, it may be said that no periods of time are specially designated. The characteristics of the relation of Christ and His Church are indicated, and we may suppose that the whole process of His exaltation from the declaration of His Sonship, by His resurrection, to the grand catastrophe of the final judgment, with all the collateral blessings to the Church and the world, lay before the vision of the inspired prophet.

Psalms 49:4.title: Psalms 49:4
Psalms 49:4.content: incline—to hear attentively (Ps 17:6; 31:2). parable—In Hebrew and Greek "parable" and "proverb" are translations of the same word. It denotes a comparison, or form of speech, which under one image includes many, and is expressive of a general truth capable of various illustrations. Hence it may be used for the illustration itself. For the former sense, "proverb" (that is, one word for several) is the usual English term, and for the latter, in which comparison is prominent, "parable" (that is, one thing laid by another). The distinction is not always observed, since here, and in Ps 78:2; "proverb" would better express the style of the composition (compare also Pr 26:7, 9; Hab 2:6; Joh 16:25, 29). Such forms of speech are often very figurative and also obscure (compare Mt 13:12-15). Hence the use of the parallel word— dark saying—or, "riddle" (compare Eze 17:2). open—is to explain. upon the harp—the accompaniment for a lyric.

Psalms 50:22.title: Psalms 50:21-22
Psalms 50:22.content: God, no longer (even in appearance) disregarding such, exposes their sins and threatens a terrible punishment.

Psalms 50:22.title: Psalms 50:22
Psalms 50:22.content: forget God—This denotes unmindfulness of His true character.

Psalms 50:23.title: Psalms 50:23
Psalms 50:23.content: offereth praise—(Ps 50:14), so that the external worship is a true index of the heart. ordereth … aright—acts in a straight, right manner, opposed to turning aside (Ps 25:5). In such, pure worship and a pure life evince their true piety, and they will enjoy God's presence and favor.

Psalms 51:1.title: Psalms 51:1-4
Psalms 51:1.content: A plea for mercy is a confession of guilt. blot out—as from a register. transgressions—literally, "rebellions" (Ps 19:13; 32:1).

Psalms 51:2.title: Psalms 51:1-4
Psalms 51:2.content: A plea for mercy is a confession of guilt. blot out—as from a register. transgressions—literally, "rebellions" (Ps 19:13; 32:1).

Psalms 51:2.title: Psalms 51:2
Psalms 51:2.content: Wash me—Purity as well as pardon is desired by true penitents.

Psalms 51:3.title: Psalms 51:1-4
Psalms 51:3.content: A plea for mercy is a confession of guilt. blot out—as from a register. transgressions—literally, "rebellions" (Ps 19:13; 32:1).

Psalms 51:3.title: Psalms 51:3
Psalms 51:3.content: For … before me—Conviction precedes forgiveness; and, as a gift of God, is a plea for it (2Sa 12:13; Ps 32:5; 1Jo 1:9).

Psalms 51:4.title: Psalms 51:1-4
Psalms 51:4.content: A plea for mercy is a confession of guilt. blot out—as from a register. transgressions—literally, "rebellions" (Ps 19:13; 32:1).

Psalms 51:4.title: Psalms 51:4
Psalms 51:4.content: Against thee—chiefly, and as sins against others are violations of God's law, in one sense only. that … judgest—that is, all palliation of his crime is excluded; it is the design in making this confession to recognize God's justice, however severe the sentence.

Psalms 51:5.title: Psalms 51:5-6
Psalms 51:5.content: His guilt was aggravated by his essential, native sinfulness, which is as contrary to God's requisitions of inward purity as are outward sins to those for right conduct.

Psalms 51:6.title: Psalms 51:5-6
Psalms 51:6.content: His guilt was aggravated by his essential, native sinfulness, which is as contrary to God's requisitions of inward purity as are outward sins to those for right conduct.

Psalms 51:6.title: Psalms 51:6
Psalms 51:6.content: thou shalt make, &c.—may be taken to express God's gracious purpose in view of His strict requisition; a purpose of which David might have availed himself as a check to his native love for sin, and, in not doing so, aggravated his guilt. truth … and …wisdom—are terms often used for piety (compare Job 28:28; Ps 119:30).

Psalms 51:7.title: Psalms 51:7-12
Psalms 51:7.content: A series of prayers for forgiveness and purifying. Purge … hyssop—The use of this plant in the ritual (Ex 12:22; Nu 19:6, 18) suggests the idea of atonement as prominent here; "purge" refers to vicarious satisfaction (Nu 19:17-20).

Psalms 51:8.title: Psalms 51:7-12
Psalms 51:8.content: A series of prayers for forgiveness and purifying. Purge … hyssop—The use of this plant in the ritual (Ex 12:22; Nu 19:6, 18) suggests the idea of atonement as prominent here; "purge" refers to vicarious satisfaction (Nu 19:17-20).

Psalms 51:8.title: Psalms 51:8
Psalms 51:8.content: Make … joy—by forgiving me, which will change distress to joy.

Psalms 51:9.title: Psalms 51:7-12
Psalms 51:9.content: A series of prayers for forgiveness and purifying. Purge … hyssop—The use of this plant in the ritual (Ex 12:22; Nu 19:6, 18) suggests the idea of atonement as prominent here; "purge" refers to vicarious satisfaction (Nu 19:17-20).

Psalms 51:10.title: Psalms 51:7-12
Psalms 51:10.content: A series of prayers for forgiveness and purifying. Purge … hyssop—The use of this plant in the ritual (Ex 12:22; Nu 19:6, 18) suggests the idea of atonement as prominent here; "purge" refers to vicarious satisfaction (Nu 19:17-20).

Psalms 51:10.title: Psalms 51:10
Psalms 51:10.content: Create—a work of almighty power. in me—literally, "to me," or, "for me"; bestow as a gift, a heart free from taint of sin (Ps 24:4; 73:1). renew—implies that he had possessed it; the essential principle of a new nature had not been lost, but its influence interrupted (Lu 22:32); for Ps 51:11 shows that he had not lost God's presence and Spirit (1Sa 16:13), though he had lost the "joy of his salvation" (Ps 51:12), for whose return he prays. right spirit—literally, "constant," "firm," not yielding to temptation.

Psalms 51:11.title: Psalms 51:7-12
Psalms 51:11.content: A series of prayers for forgiveness and purifying. Purge … hyssop—The use of this plant in the ritual (Ex 12:22; Nu 19:6, 18) suggests the idea of atonement as prominent here; "purge" refers to vicarious satisfaction (Nu 19:17-20).

Psalms 51:12.title: Psalms 51:7-12
Psalms 51:12.content: A series of prayers for forgiveness and purifying. Purge … hyssop—The use of this plant in the ritual (Ex 12:22; Nu 19:6, 18) suggests the idea of atonement as prominent here; "purge" refers to vicarious satisfaction (Nu 19:17-20).

Psalms 51:12.title: Psalms 51:12
Psalms 51:12.content: free spirit—"thy" ought not to be supplied, for the word "free" is, literally, "willing," and "spirit" is that of David. "Let a willing spirit uphold me," that is, with a soul willingly conformed to God's law, he would be preserved in a right course of conduct.

Psalms 51:13.title: Psalms 51:13
Psalms 51:13.content: Then—Such will be the effect of this gracious work. ways—of providence and human duty (Ps 18:21, 30; 32:8; Lu 22:32).

Psalms 51:14.title: Psalms 51:14
Psalms 51:14.content: Deliver—or, "Free me" (Ps 39:8) from the guilt of murder (2Sa 12:9, 10; Ps 5:6). righteousness—as in Ps 7:17; 31:1.

Psalms 51:15.title: Psalms 51:15
Psalms 51:15.content: open … lips—by removing my sense of guilt.

Psalms 51:16.title: Psalms 51:16
Psalms 51:16.content: Praise is better than sacrifice (Ps 50:14), and implying faith, penitence, and love, glorifies God. In true penitents the joys of pardon mingle with sorrow for sin.

Psalms 51:18.title: Psalms 51:18
Psalms 51:18.content: Do good, &c.—Visit not my sin on Thy Church. build … walls—is to show favor; compare Ps 89:40, for opposite form and idea.

Psalms 51:19.title: Psalms 51:19
Psalms 51:19.content: God reconciled, material sacrifices will be acceptable (Ps 4:5; compare Isa 1:11-17).

Psalms 52:1.title: Psalms 52:1
Psalms 52:1.content: mighty man—literally, "hero." Doeg may be thus addressed, ironically, in respect of his might in slander.

Psalms 52:2.title: Psalms 52:2
Psalms 52:2.content: tongue—for self. mischiefs—evil to others (Ps 5:9; 38:12). working deceitfully—(Ps 10:7), as a keen, smoothly moving razor, cutting quietly, but deeply.

Psalms 52:5.title: Psalms 52:5
Psalms 52:5.content: likewise—or, "so," "also," as you have done to others God will do to you (Ps 18:27). The following terms describe the most entire ruin.

Psalms 52:6.title: Psalms 52:6
Psalms 52:6.content: shall … fear—regard with religious awe. laugh at him—for his folly;

Psalms 52:7.title: Psalms 52:7
Psalms 52:7.content: for trusting in riches and being strong in "wickedness." wickedness—literally, "mischief" (Ps 52:2), instead of trusting in God. the man—literally, "the mighty man," or "hero" (Ps 52:1).

Psalms 52:8.title: Psalms 52:8
Psalms 52:8.content: The figure used is common (Ps 1:3; Jer 11:16). green—fresh. house, &c.—in communion with God (compare Ps 27:4, 5). for ever and ever—qualifies "mercy."

Psalms 52:9.title: Psalms 52:9
Psalms 52:9.content: hast done—that is, what the context supplies, "preserved me" (compare Ps 22:31). wait … name—hope in Thy perfections, manifested for my good (Ps 5:11; 20:1). for it is good—that is, Thy name, and the whole method or result of its manifestation (Ps 54:6; 69:16).

Psalms 53:1.title: Psalms 53:1-4
Psalms 53:1.content: with few verbal changes, correspond with Ps 14:1-4.

Psalms 53:2.title: Psalms 53:1-4
Psalms 53:2.content: with few verbal changes, correspond with Ps 14:1-4.

Psalms 53:3.title: Psalms 53:1-4
Psalms 53:3.content: with few verbal changes, correspond with Ps 14:1-4.

Psalms 53:4.title: Psalms 53:1-4
Psalms 53:4.content: with few verbal changes, correspond with Ps 14:1-4.

Psalms 53:5.title: Psalms 53:5
Psalms 53:5.content: Instead of assurances of God's presence with the pious, and a complaint of the wicked, Ps 14:5, 6 portrays the ruin of the latter, whose "bones" even "are scattered" (compare Ps 141:7), and who are put to shame as contemptuously rejected of God.

Psalms 54:1.title: Psalms 54:1
Psalms 54:1.content: by thy name—(Ps 5:11), specially, power. judge me—as in Ps 7:8; 26:1.

Psalms 54:3.title: Psalms 54:3
Psalms 54:3.content: strangers—perhaps Ziphites. oppressors—literally, "terrible ones" (Isa 13:11; 25:3). Such were Saul and his army. not set … them—acted as atheists, without God's fear (compare Ps 16:8).

Psalms 54:4.title: Psalms 54:4
Psalms 54:4.content: (Compare Ps 30:10). with them—on their side, and for me (compare Ps 46:11).

Psalms 54:5.title: Psalms 54:5
Psalms 54:5.content: He shall … evil—or, "Evil shall return on" (Ps 7:16) my enemies or watchers, that is, to do me evil (Ps 6:7). in thy truth—Thy verified promise.

Psalms 54:6.title: Psalms 54:6
Psalms 54:6.content: I will freely, &c.—or, present a freewill offering (Le 7:16; Nu 15:3).

Psalms 54:7.title: Psalms 54:7
Psalms 54:7.content: mine eye … desire—(compare Ps 59:10; 112:8), expresses satisfaction in beholding the overthrow of his enemies as those of God, without implying any selfish or unholy feeling (compare Ps 52:6, 7).

Psalms 55:1.title: Psalms 55:1
Psalms 55:1.content: hide not thyself, &c.—(compare Ps 13:1; 27:9), withhold not help.

Psalms 55:2.title: Psalms 55:2
Psalms 55:2.content: The terms of the last clause express full indulgence of grief.

Psalms 55:3.title: Psalms 55:3
Psalms 55:3.content: oppression—literally, "persecution." they … iniquity—literally, "they make evil doings slide upon me."

Psalms 55:6.title: Psalms 55:6
Psalms 55:6.content: be at rest—literally, "dwell," that is, permanently.

Psalms 55:7.title: Psalms 55:7-8
Psalms 55:7.content: Even a wilderness is a safer place than exposure to such evils, terrible as storm and tempest.

Psalms 55:8.title: Psalms 55:7-8
Psalms 55:8.content: Even a wilderness is a safer place than exposure to such evils, terrible as storm and tempest.

Psalms 55:9.title: Psalms 55:9
Psalms 55:9.content: Destroy—literally, "swallow" (Ps 21:9). divide their tongues—or, "confound their speech," and hence their counsels (Ge 11:7). the city—perhaps Jerusalem, the scene of anarchy.

Psalms 55:10.title: Psalms 55:10-11
Psalms 55:10.content: which is described in detail (compare Ps 7:14-16).

Psalms 55:11.title: Psalms 55:10-11
Psalms 55:11.content: which is described in detail (compare Ps 7:14-16).

Psalms 55:11.title: Psalms 55:11
Psalms 55:11.content: Wickedness—literally, "Mischief," evils resulting from others (Ps 5:9; 52:2, 7). streets—or literally, "wide places," markets, courts of justice, and any public place.

Psalms 55:12.title: Psalms 55:12-14
Psalms 55:12.content: This description of treachery does not deny, but aggravates, the injury from enemies.

Psalms 55:13.title: Psalms 55:12-14
Psalms 55:13.content: This description of treachery does not deny, but aggravates, the injury from enemies.

Psalms 55:13.title: Psalms 55:13
Psalms 55:13.content: guide—literally, "friend" (Pr 16:28; 17:9). acquaintance—in Hebrew, a yet more intimate associate.

Psalms 55:14.title: Psalms 55:12-14
Psalms 55:14.content: This description of treachery does not deny, but aggravates, the injury from enemies.

Psalms 55:14.title: Psalms 55:14
Psalms 55:14.content: in company—literally, "with a crowd," in a festal procession.

Psalms 55:15.title: Psalms 55:15
Psalms 55:15.content: Let death, &c.—or, "Desolations are on them." let them go—literally, "they will go." quick—or, living in the midst of life, death will come (compare Nu 16:33). among them—or, "within them," in their hearts (Ps 5:9; 49:11).

Psalms 55:16.title: Psalms 55:16-18
Psalms 55:16.content: God answers his constant and repeated prayers.

Psalms 55:17.title: Psalms 55:16-18
Psalms 55:17.content: God answers his constant and repeated prayers.

Psalms 55:18.title: Psalms 55:16-18
Psalms 55:18.content: God answers his constant and repeated prayers.

Psalms 55:18.title: Psalms 55:18
Psalms 55:18.content: many with me—that is, by the context, fighting with me.

Psalms 55:19.title: Psalms 55:19
Psalms 55:19.content: God hears the wicked in wrath. abideth—or, "sitteth." of old—enthroned as a sovereign. Because … no changes—Prosperity hardens them (Ps 73:5).

Psalms 55:20.title: Psalms 55:20-21
Psalms 55:20.content: The treachery is aggravated by hypocrisy. The changes of number, Ps 55:15, 23, and here, enliven the picture, and imply that the chief traitor and his accomplices are in view together.

Psalms 55:21.title: Psalms 55:20-21
Psalms 55:21.content: The treachery is aggravated by hypocrisy. The changes of number, Ps 55:15, 23, and here, enliven the picture, and imply that the chief traitor and his accomplices are in view together.

Psalms 55:22.title: Psalms 55:22
Psalms 55:22.content: thy burden—literally, "gift," what is assigned you. he shall sustain—literally, "supply food," and so all need (Ps 37:25; Mt 6:11). to be moved—from the secure position of His favor (compare Ps 10:6).

Psalms 55:23.title: Psalms 55:23
Psalms 55:23.content: bloody … days—(compare Ps 5:6; 51:14), deceit and murderous dispositions often united. The threat is directed specially (not as a general truth) against the wicked, then in the writer's view.

Psalms 56:1.title: Psalms 56:1-2
Psalms 56:1.content: would swallow—literally, "pants as a raging beast" (Ac 9:1).

Psalms 56:2.title: Psalms 56:1-2
Psalms 56:2.content: would swallow—literally, "pants as a raging beast" (Ac 9:1).

Psalms 56:2.title: Psalms 56:2
Psalms 56:2.content: enemies—watchers (Ps 54:5). most High—As it is not elsewhere used absolutely for God, some render the word here, arrogantly, or proudly, as qualifying "those who fight," &c.

Psalms 56:3.title: Psalms 56:3
Psalms 56:3.content: in—or literally, "unto." thee—to whom he turns in trouble.

Psalms 56:4.title: Psalms 56:4
Psalms 56:4.content: in God … his word—By His grace or aid (Ps 60:12; 108:13), or, "I will boast in God as to His word"; in either case His word is the special matter and cause of praise. flesh—for mankind (Ps 65:2; Isa 31:3), intimating frailty.

Psalms 56:5.title: Psalms 56:5-6
Psalms 56:5.content: A vivid picture of the conduct of malicious enemies.

Psalms 56:6.title: Psalms 56:5-6
Psalms 56:6.content: A vivid picture of the conduct of malicious enemies.

Psalms 56:7.title: Psalms 56:7
Psalms 56:7.content: Shall they escape? &c.—or better, "Their escape is by iniquity." cast … people—humble those who so proudly oppose Thy servant.

Psalms 56:8.title: Psalms 56:8
Psalms 56:8.content: God is mindful of his exile and remembers his tears. The custom of bottling the tears of mourners as a memorial, which has existed in some Eastern nations, may explain the figure.

Psalms 56:9.title: Psalms 56:9
Psalms 56:9.content: God is for me—or, "on my side" (Ps 118:6; 124:1, 2); hence he is sure of the repulse of his foes.

Psalms 56:12.title: Psalms 56:12
Psalms 56:12.content: I will render praises—will pay what I have vowed.

Psalms 56:13.title: Psalms 56:13
Psalms 56:13.content: The question implies an affirmative answer, drawn from past experience. falling—as from a precipice. before God—in His favor during life.

Psalms 57:1.title: Psalms 57:1
Psalms 57:1.content: my soul—or self, or life, which is threatened. shadow of thy wings—(Ps 17:8; 36:7). calamities—literally, "mischiefs" (Ps 52:2; 55:10).

Psalms 57:2.title: Psalms 57:2
Psalms 57:2.content: performeth—or, completes what He has begun.

Psalms 57:3.title: Psalms 57:3
Psalms 57:3.content: from … swallow me up—that pants in rage after me (Ps 56:2). mercy and … truth—(Ps 25:10; 36:5), as messengers (Ps 43:3) sent to deliver him.

Psalms 57:4.title: Psalms 57:4
Psalms 57:4.content: The mingled figures of wild beasts (Ps 10:9; 17:12) and weapons of war (Ps 11:2) heighten the picture of danger. whose … tongue—or slanders.

Psalms 57:5.title: Psalms 57:5
Psalms 57:5.content: This doxology illustrates his view of the connection of his deliverance with God's glory.

Psalms 57:7.title: Psalms 57:7
Psalms 57:7.content: I will … praise—both with voice and instrument.

Psalms 57:8.title: Psalms 57:8
Psalms 57:8.content: Hence—he addresses his glory, or tongue (Ps 16:9; 30:12), and his psaltery, or lute, and harp. I myself … early—literally, "I will awaken dawn," poetically expressing his zeal and diligence.

Psalms 57:9.title: Psalms 57:9-10
Psalms 57:9.content: As His mercy and truth, so shall His praise, fill the universe.

Psalms 57:10.title: Psalms 57:9-10
Psalms 57:10.content: As His mercy and truth, so shall His praise, fill the universe.

Psalms 58:1.title: Psalms 58:1
Psalms 58:1.content: O congregation—literally, "Oh, dumb"; the word used is never translated "congregation." "Are ye dumb? ye should speak righteousness," may be the translation. In any case, the writer remonstrates with them, perhaps a council, who were assembled to try his cause, and bound to give a right decision.

Psalms 58:2.title: Psalms 58:2
Psalms 58:2.content: This they did not design; but weigh … violence—or give decisions of violence. Weigh is a figure to express the acts of judges. in the earth—publicly.

Psalms 58:3.title: Psalms 58:3-5
Psalms 58:3.content: describe the wicked generally, who sin naturally, easily, malignantly, and stubbornly.

Psalms 58:4.title: Psalms 58:3-5
Psalms 58:4.content: describe the wicked generally, who sin naturally, easily, malignantly, and stubbornly.

Psalms 58:4.title: Psalms 58:4
Psalms 58:4.content: stoppeth her—literally, "his." ear—that is, the wicked man (the singular used collectively), who thus becomes like the deaf adder which has no ear.

Psalms 58:5.title: Psalms 58:3-5
Psalms 58:5.content: describe the wicked generally, who sin naturally, easily, malignantly, and stubbornly.

Psalms 58:6.title: Psalms 58:6
Psalms 58:6.content: He prays for their destruction, under the figure of ravenous beasts (Ps 3:7; 7:2).

Psalms 58:7.title: Psalms 58:7
Psalms 58:7.content: which run continually—literally, "they shall go to themselves," utterly depart, as rapid mountain torrents. he bendeth … his arrows—prepares it. The term for preparing a bow applied to arrows (Ps 64:3). let them … pieces—literally, "as if they cut themselves off"—that is, become blunted and of no avail.

Psalms 58:8.title: Psalms 58:8-9
Psalms 58:8.content: Other figures of this utter ruin; the last denoting rapidity. In a shorter time than pots feel the heat of thorns on fire—

Psalms 58:9.title: Psalms 58:8-9
Psalms 58:9.content: Other figures of this utter ruin; the last denoting rapidity. In a shorter time than pots feel the heat of thorns on fire—

Psalms 58:9.title: Psalms 58:9
Psalms 58:9.content: he shall take them away as with a whirlwind—literally, "blow him (them) away." both living … wrath—literally, "as the living" or fresh as the heated or burning—that is, thorns—all easily blown away, so easily and quickly the wicked. The figure of the "snail" perhaps alludes to its loss of saliva when moving. Though obscure in its clauses, the general sense of the passage is clear.

Psalms 58:10.title: Psalms 58:10-11
Psalms 58:10.content: wash … wicked—denoting great slaughter. The joy of triumph over the destruction of the wicked is because they are God's enemies, and their overthrow shows that He reigneth (compare Ps 52:5-7; 54:7). In this assurance let heaven and earth rejoice (Ps 96:10; 97:1, &c.).

Psalms 58:11.title: Psalms 58:10-11
Psalms 58:11.content: wash … wicked—denoting great slaughter. The joy of triumph over the destruction of the wicked is because they are God's enemies, and their overthrow shows that He reigneth (compare Ps 52:5-7; 54:7). In this assurance let heaven and earth rejoice (Ps 96:10; 97:1, &c.).

Psalms 59:1.title: Psalms 59:1
Psalms 59:1.content: defend me—(Compare Margin). rise up … me—(Compare Ps 17:7).

Psalms 59:4.title: Psalms 59:4-5
Psalms 59:4.content: prepare, &c.—literally, "set themselves as in array." awake—(Compare Ps 3:7; 7:6), appeals to God in His covenant relation to His people (Ps 9:18).

Psalms 59:5.title: Psalms 59:4-5
Psalms 59:5.content: prepare, &c.—literally, "set themselves as in array." awake—(Compare Ps 3:7; 7:6), appeals to God in His covenant relation to His people (Ps 9:18).

Psalms 59:6.title: Psalms 59:6-7
Psalms 59:6.content: They are as ravening dogs seeking prey, and as such, belch out—that is, slanders, their impudent barkings.

Psalms 59:7.title: Psalms 59:6-7
Psalms 59:7.content: They are as ravening dogs seeking prey, and as such, belch out—that is, slanders, their impudent barkings.

Psalms 59:7.title: Psalms 59:7
Psalms 59:7.content: for who, say they—For the full expression with the supplied words, compare Ps 64:5.

Psalms 59:9.title: Psalms 59:9
Psalms 59:9.content: By judicious expositors, and on good grounds, this is better rendered, "O my strength, on Thee will I wait" (Ps 59:17). defence—(Compare Ps 18:3).

Psalms 59:10.title: Psalms 59:10
Psalms 59:10.content: prevent me—(Ps 21:3). see my desire—in their overthrow (Ps 54:7). enemies—as in Ps 5:8.

Psalms 59:11.title: Psalms 59:11
Psalms 59:11.content: Slay them not—at once (Jud 2:21-23); but perpetuate their punishment (Ge 4:12; Nu 32:13), by scattering or making them wander, and humble them.

Psalms 59:12.title: Psalms 59:12
Psalms 59:12.content: let them even be … taken in their pride—while evincing it—that is, to be punished for their lies, &c.

Psalms 59:13.title: Psalms 59:13
Psalms 59:13.content: Though delayed for wise reasons, the utter destruction of the wicked must come at last, and God's presence and power in and for His Church will be known abroad (1Sa 17:46; Ps 46:10, 11).

Psalms 59:14.title: Psalms 59:14-15
Psalms 59:14.content: Meanwhile let the rapacious dogs prowl, they cannot hurt the pious; yea, they shall wander famished and sleepless.

Psalms 59:15.title: Psalms 59:14-15
Psalms 59:15.content: Meanwhile let the rapacious dogs prowl, they cannot hurt the pious; yea, they shall wander famished and sleepless.

Psalms 59:15.title: Psalms 59:15
Psalms 59:15.content: grudge if, &c.—literally, "they shall stay all night," that is, obtain nothing.

Psalms 59:16.title: Psalms 59:16-17
Psalms 59:16.content: Contrast the lot of God's servant, who employs his time in God's praise. sing aloud … in the morning—when they retire famishing and disappointed, or it may denote delightful diligence in praise, as in Ps 30:5.

Psalms 59:17.title: Psalms 59:16-17
Psalms 59:17.content: Contrast the lot of God's servant, who employs his time in God's praise. sing aloud … in the morning—when they retire famishing and disappointed, or it may denote delightful diligence in praise, as in Ps 30:5.

Psalms 60:1.title: Psalms 60:1-3
Psalms 60:1.content: allude to disasters. cast … off—in scorn (Ps 43:2; 44:9). scattered—broken our strength (compare 2Sa 5:20). Oh, turn thyself—or, "restore to us" (prosperity). The figures of physical, denote great civil, commotions (Ps 46:2, 3).

Psalms 60:2.title: Psalms 60:1-3
Psalms 60:2.content: allude to disasters. cast … off—in scorn (Ps 43:2; 44:9). scattered—broken our strength (compare 2Sa 5:20). Oh, turn thyself—or, "restore to us" (prosperity). The figures of physical, denote great civil, commotions (Ps 46:2, 3).

Psalms 60:3.title: Psalms 60:3
Psalms 60:3.content: drink … wine of astonishment—literally, "of staggering"—that is, made us weak (compare Ps 75:8; Isa 51:17, 22).

Psalms 60:4.title: Psalms 60:4-5
Psalms 60:4.content: Yet to God's banner they will rally, and pray that, led and sustained by His power (right hand, Ps 17:7; 20:6), they may be safe.

Shechem, and … Succoth—as widely separated points, and—

Ephraim—denotes the military (De 33:17); and— Judah—(the lawgiver, Ge 49:10), the civil power. Foreign nations are then presented as subdued.

Psalms 60:8.content: Moab—is a my washpot—the most ordinary vessel. over—or, "at" Edom—(as a slave) he casts his shoe. Philistia, triumph, &c.—or, rather, "shout." for me—acknowledges subjection (compare Ps 108:9, "over Philistia will I triumph").

Psalms 60:11.title: Psalms 60:11-12
Psalms 60:11.content: Hence he closes with a prayer for success, and an assurance of a hearing.

Psalms 61:1.title: Psalms 61:1-3
Psalms 61:1.content: From the end—that is, places remote from the sanctuary (De 28:64).

Psalms 61:2.title: Psalms 61:1-3
Psalms 61:2.content: From the end—that is, places remote from the sanctuary (De 28:64).

Psalms 61:2.title: Psalms 61:2
Psalms 61:2.content: heart is overwhelmed—literally, "covered over with darkness," or, "distress." to the rock—(Ps 18:2; 40:2). higher than I—which otherwise I cannot ascend.

Psalms 61:3.title: Psalms 61:1-3
Psalms 61:3.content: From the end—that is, places remote from the sanctuary (De 28:64).

Psalms 61:3.title: Psalms 61:3
Psalms 61:3.content: shelter … and strong tower—repeat the same sentiment.

Psalms 61:4.title: Psalms 61:4
Psalms 61:4.content: I will abide—So I desire to do (compare Ps 23:6). trust in the covert, &c.—make my refuge, in the shadow (compare Ps 17:8; 36:7).

Psalms 61:5.title: Psalms 61:5
Psalms 61:5.content: the heritage—or, part in the spiritual blessings of Israel (Ps 21:2-4). vows—implies prayers.

Psalms 61:6.title: Psalms 61:6-7
Psalms 61:6.content: the king—himself and his royal line ending in Christ. Mercy and truth personified, as in Ps 40:11; 57:3.

Psalms 61:7.title: Psalms 61:6-7
Psalms 61:7.content: the king—himself and his royal line ending in Christ. Mercy and truth personified, as in Ps 40:11; 57:3.

Psalms 61:7.title: Psalms 61:7
Psalms 61:7.content: abide before God—literally, "sit as a king in God's presence," under His protection.

Psalms 61:8.title: Psalms 61:8
Psalms 61:8.content: Thus for new blessings will new vows of praise ever be paid.

Psalms 62:1.title: Psalms 62:1
Psalms 62:1.content: waiteth—literally, "is silent," trusts submissively and confidently as a servant.

Psalms 62:2.title: Psalms 62:2
Psalms 62:2.content: The titles applied to God often occur (Ps 9:9; 18:2). be greatly moved—(Ps 10:6). No injury shall be permanent, though devised by enemies.

Psalms 62:3.title: Psalms 62:3
Psalms 62:3.content: Their destruction will come; as a tottering wall they already are feeble and failing. bowing wall shall ye be—better supply "are." Some propose to apply these phrases to describe the condition of "a man"—that is, the pious suffer: thus, "Will ye slay him," &c.; but the other is a good sense.

Psalms 62:4.title: Psalms 62:4
Psalms 62:4.content: his excellency—or, elevation to which God had raised him (Ps 4:2). This they try to do by lies and duplicity (Ps 5:9).

Psalms 62:6.title: Psalms 62:6
Psalms 62:6.content: not be moved—not at all; his confidence has increased.

Psalms 62:7.title: Psalms 62:7
Psalms 62:7.content: rock of my strength—or strongest support (Ps 7:10; 61:3).

Psalms 62:8.title: Psalms 62:8
Psalms 62:8.content: pour out your heart—give full expression to feeling (1Sa 1:15; Job 30:16; Ps 42:4). ye people—God's people.

Psalms 62:9.title: Psalms 62:9
Psalms 62:9.content: No kind of men are reliable, compared with God (Isa 2:22; Jer 17:5). altogether—alike, one as the other (Ps 34:3).

Psalms 62:10.title: Psalms 62:10
Psalms 62:10.content: Not only are oppression and robbery, which are wicked means of wealth, no grounds of boasting; but even wealth, increasing lawfully, ought not to engross the heart.

Psalms 62:11.title: Psalms 62:11
Psalms 62:11.content: once; twice—(as in Job 33:14; 40:5), are used to give emphasis to the sentiment. God's power is tempered by His mercy, which it also sustains.

Psalms 62:12.title: Psalms 62:12
Psalms 62:12.content: for thou renderest—literally, "that Thou renderest," &c., connected with "I heard this," as the phrase—"that power," &c. [Ps 62:11]—teaching that by His power He can show both mercy and justice.

Psalms 63:1.title: Psalms 63:1
Psalms 63:1.content: early … seek thee—earnestly (Isa 26:9). The figurative terms— dry and thirsty—literally, "weary," denoting moral destitution, suited his outward circumstances. soul—and—flesh—the whole man (Ps 16:9, 10).

Psalms 63:2.title: Psalms 63:2
Psalms 63:2.content: The special object of desire was God's perfections as displayed in his worship (Ps 27:4).

Psalms 63:3.title: Psalms 63:3
Psalms 63:3.content: Experiencing God's mercy, which exceeds all the blessings of life, his lips will be opened for his praise (Ps 51:15).

Psalms 63:4.title: Psalms 63:4
Psalms 63:4.content: Thus—literally, "Truly." will I bless—praise Thee (Ps 34:1). lift up my hands—in worship (compare Ps 28:2). in thy name—in praise of Thy perfections.

Psalms 63:5.title: Psalms 63:5-8
Psalms 63:5.content: Full spiritual blessings satisfy his desires, and acts of praise fill his thoughts and time.

Psalms 63:6.title: Psalms 63:5-8
Psalms 63:6.content: Full spiritual blessings satisfy his desires, and acts of praise fill his thoughts and time.

Psalms 63:6.title: Psalms 63:6
Psalms 63:6.content: night—as well as day. Past favors assure him of future, and hence he presses earnestly near to God, whose power sustains him (Ps 17:8; 60:5).

Psalms 63:7.title: Psalms 63:5-8
Psalms 63:7.content: Full spiritual blessings satisfy his desires, and acts of praise fill his thoughts and time.

Psalms 63:10.title: Psalms 63:9-10
Psalms 63:10.content: those … to destroy it—or literally, "to ruin," or, "for ruin"; that is, such as seek to injure me (are) for ruin, appointed to it (compare Ps 35:8). shall go … earth—into the grave, or, to death; as their bodies are represented as a portion for—

Psalms 63:11.title: Psalms 63:11
Psalms 63:11.content: the king—that is, David himself, and all who reverence God, "shall share a glorious part," while treacherous foes shall be for ever silenced (Ps 62:4).

Psalms 64:1.title: Psalms 64:1
Psalms 64:1.content: preserve … fear—as well as the danger producing it.

Psalms 64:2.title: Psalms 64:2
Psalms 64:2.content: insurrection—literally, "uproar," noisy assaults, as well as their secret counsels.

Psalms 64:3.title: Psalms 64:3-4
Psalms 64:3.content: Similar figures for slander (Ps 57:4; 59:7). bend—literally, "tread," or, "prepared." The allusion is to the mode of bending a bow by treading on it; here, and in Ps 58:7, transferred to arrows.

Psalms 64:4.title: Psalms 64:3-4

Psalms 64:4.title: Psalms 64:4
Psalms 64:4.content: the perfect—one innocent of the charges made (Ps 18:23). fear not—(Ps 55:19), not regarding God.

Psalms 64:5.title: Psalms 64:5
Psalms 64:5.content: A sentiment here more fully presented, by depicting their deliberate malice.

Psalms 64:6.title: Psalms 64:6
Psalms 64:6.content: This is further evinced by their diligent efforts and deeply laid schemes.

Psalms 64:7.title: Psalms 64:7
Psalms 64:7.content: The contrast is heightened by representing God as using weapons like theirs.

Psalms 64:8.title: Psalms 64:8
Psalms 64:8.content: their … tongue to fall, &c.—that is, the consequences of their slanders, &c. (compare Ps 10:2; 31:16). all that see … away—Their partners in evil shall be terrified.

Psalms 64:9.title: Psalms 64:9-10
Psalms 64:9.content: Men, generally, will acknowledge God's work, and the righteous, rejoicing in it, shall be encouraged to trust Him (Ps 58:10).

Psalms 65:1.title: Psalms 65:1
Psalms 65:1.content: Praise waiteth for thee—literally, "To Thee silence praise," or (compare Ps 62:1), To Thee silence is praise—that is, Praise is waiting as a servant; it is due to Thee. So the last clause expresses the duty of paying vows. These two parts of acceptable worship, mentioned in Ps 50:14, are rendered in Zion, where God chiefly displays His mercy and receives homage.

Psalms 65:2.title: Psalms 65:2
Psalms 65:2.content: All are encouraged to pray by God's readiness to hear.

Psalms 65:3.title: Psalms 65:3
Psalms 65:3.content: God's mercy alone delivers us from the burden of iniquities, by purging or expiating by an atonement the transgressions with which we are charged, and which are denoted by— Iniquities—or, literally, "Words of iniquities."

Psalms 65:4.title: Psalms 65:4
Psalms 65:4.content: dwell in thy courts; … [and] satisfied with the goodness … temple—denote communion with God (Ps 15:1; 23:6; compare Ps 5:7). This is a blessing for all God's people, as denoted by the change of number.

Psalms 65:5.title: Psalms 65:5
Psalms 65:5.content: terrible things—that is, by the manifestation of justice and wrath to enemies, accompanying that of mercy to His people (Ps 63:9-11; 64:7-9). the confidence—object of it. of all … earth—the whole world; that is, deservedly such, whether men think so or not.

Psalms 65:6.title: Psalms 65:6-13
Psalms 65:6.content: God's great power and goodness are the grounds of this confidence. These are illustrated in His control of the mightiest agencies of nature and nations affecting men with awe and dread (Ps 26:7; 98:1, &c.), and in His fertilizing showers, causing the earth to produce abundantly for man and beast.

Psalms 65:12.title: Psalms 65:12
Psalms 65:12.content: wilderness—places, though not inhabited by men, fit for pasture (Le 16:21, 22; Job 24:5). pastures—is literally, "folds," or "enclosures for flocks"; and in Ps 65:13 it may be "lambs," the same word used and so translated in Ps 37:20; so that "the flocks are clothed with lambs" (a figure for abundant increase) would be the form of expression.

Psalms 66:2.title: Psalms 66:2
Psalms 66:2.content: his name—as in Ps 29:2. make his praise glorious—literally, "place honor, His praise," or, "as to His praise"; that is, let His praise be such as will glorify Him, or, be honorable to Him.

Psalms 66:3.title: Psalms 66:3-4
Psalms 66:3.content: A specimen of the praise. How terrible—(Compare Ps 65:8). submit—(Compare Margin), show a forced subjection (Ps 18:44), produced by terror.

Psalms 66:4.title: Psalms 66:3-4
Psalms 66:4.content: A specimen of the praise. How terrible—(Compare Ps 65:8). submit—(Compare Margin), show a forced subjection (Ps 18:44), produced by terror.

Psalms 66:5.title: Psalms 66:5-6
Psalms 66:5.content: The terrible works illustrated in Israel's history (Ex 14:21). By this example let rebels be admonished.

Psalms 66:6.title: Psalms 66:5-6
Psalms 66:6.content: The terrible works illustrated in Israel's history (Ex 14:21). By this example let rebels be admonished.

Psalms 66:8.title: Psalms 66:8-9
Psalms 66:8.content: Here is, perhaps, cited a case of recent deliverance.

Psalms 66:9.title: Psalms 66:8-9
Psalms 66:9.content: Here is, perhaps, cited a case of recent deliverance.

Psalms 66:9.title: Psalms 66:9
Psalms 66:9.content: holdeth … in life—literally, "putteth our soul in life"; that is, out of danger (Ps 30:3; 49:15). to be moved—(Compare Ps 10:6; 55:22).

Psalms 66:10.title: Psalms 66:10-12
Psalms 66:10.content: Out of severe trials, God had brought them to safety (compare Isa 48:10; 1Pe 1:7).

Psalms 66:11.title: Psalms 66:10-12
Psalms 66:11.content: Out of severe trials, God had brought them to safety (compare Isa 48:10; 1Pe 1:7).

Psalms 66:11.title: Psalms 66:11
Psalms 66:11.content: affliction—literally, "pressure," or, as in Ps 55:3, "oppression," which, laid on the loins—the seat of strength (De 33:11), enfeebles the frame.

Psalms 66:12.title: Psalms 66:10-12
Psalms 66:12.content: Out of severe trials, God had brought them to safety (compare Isa 48:10; 1Pe 1:7).

Psalms 66:12.title: Psalms 66:12
Psalms 66:12.content: men to ride over our heads—made us to pass. through fire, &c.—figures describing prostration and critical dangers (compare Isa 43:2; Eze 36:12). wealthy—literally, "overflowing," or, "irrigated," and hence fertile.

Psalms 66:13.title: Psalms 66:13-15
Psalms 66:13.content: These full and varied offerings constitute the payment of vows (Le 22:18-23).

Psalms 66:14.title: Psalms 66:13-15
Psalms 66:14.content: These full and varied offerings constitute the payment of vows (Le 22:18-23).

Psalms 66:15.title: Psalms 66:13-15
Psalms 66:15.content: These full and varied offerings constitute the payment of vows (Le 22:18-23).

Psalms 66:15.title: Psalms 66:15
Psalms 66:15.content: I will offer—literally, "make to ascend," alluding to the smoke of burnt offering, which explains the use of "incense." incense—elsewhere always denoting the fumes of aromatics.

Psalms 66:16.title: Psalms 66:16-20
Psalms 66:16.content: With these he unites his public thanks, inviting those who fear God (Ps 60:4; 61:5, His true worshippers) to hear. He vindicates his sincerity, inasmuch as God would not hear hypocrites, but had heard him.

Psalms 66:17.title: Psalms 66:16-20
Psalms 66:17.content: With these he unites his public thanks, inviting those who fear God (Ps 60:4; 61:5, His true worshippers) to hear. He vindicates his sincerity, inasmuch as God would not hear hypocrites, but had heard him.

Psalms 66:17.title: Psalms 66:17
Psalms 66:17.content: he was extolled with my tongue—literally, "exaltation (was) under my tongue," as a place of deposit, whence it proceeded; that is, honoring God was habitual.

Psalms 66:18.title: Psalms 66:16-20
Psalms 66:18.content: With these he unites his public thanks, inviting those who fear God (Ps 60:4; 61:5, His true worshippers) to hear. He vindicates his sincerity, inasmuch as God would not hear hypocrites, but had heard him.

Psalms 66:18.title: Psalms 66:18
Psalms 66:18.content: If I regard iniquity in my heart—literally, "see iniquity with pleasure."

Psalms 67:1.content: cause his face to shine—show us favor (Nu 6:24, 25; Ps 31:16).

Psalms 67:2.title: Psalms 67:2
Psalms 67:2.content: thy way—of gracious dealing (Isa 55:8), as explained by— saving health—or literally, "salvation."

Psalms 67:3.title: Psalms 67:3-5
Psalms 67:3.content: Thanks will be rendered for the blessings of His wise and holy government (compare Isa 2:3, 4; 11:4).

Psalms 67:4.content: Thanks will be rendered for the blessings of His wise and holy government (compare Isa 2:3, 4; 11:4).

Psalms 67:6.title: Psalms 67:6-7
Psalms 67:6.content: The blessings of a fruitful harvest are mentioned as types of greater and spiritual blessings, under which all nations shall fear and love God.

Psalms 67:7.content: The blessings of a fruitful harvest are mentioned as types of greater and spiritual blessings, under which all nations shall fear and love God.

Psalms 68:13.content: Some translate this, "When ye shall lie between the borders, ye shall," &c., comparing the peaceful rest in the borders or limits of the promised land to the proverbial beauty of a gentle dove. Others understand by the word rendered "pots," the smoked sides of caves, in which the Israelites took refuge from enemies in the times of the judges; or, taking the whole figuratively, the rows of stones on which cooking vessels were hung; and thus that a contrast is drawn between their former low and afflicted state and their succeeding prosperity. Psalms 68:16.title: Psalms 68:15-16

Psalms 68:17.title: Psalms 68:17
Psalms 68:17.content: and, to the assertion of God's purpose to make it His dwelling, is added evidence of His protecting care. He is described as in the midst of His heavenly armies— thousands of angels—literally, "thousands of repetitions," or, "thousands of thousands"—that is, of chariots. The word "angels" was perhaps introduced in our version, from De 33:2, and Ga 3:19. They are, of course, implied as conductors of the chariots. as … Sinai, in the holy place—that is, He has appeared in Zion as once in Sinai.

Psalms 68:18.title: Psalms 68:18
Psalms 68:18.content: From the scene of conquest He ascends to His throne, leading— captivity captive—or, "many captives captive" (Jud 5:12). received gifts for men—accepting their homage, even when forced, as that of rebels. that the Lord God might dwell—or literally, "to dwell, O Lord God" (compare Ps 68:16)—that is, to make this hill, His people or Church, His dwelling. This Psalm typifies the conquests of the Church under her divine leader, Christ. He, indeed, "who was with the Church in the wilderness" (Ac 7:38) is the Lord, described in this ideal ascension. Hence Paul (Eph 4:8) applies this language to describe His real ascension, when, having conquered sin, death, and hell, the Lord of glory triumphantly entered heaven, attended by throngs of adoring angels, to sit on the throne and wield the scepter of an eternal dominion. The phrase "received gifts for (or literally, among) men" is by Paul, "gave gifts to men." Both describe the acts of a conqueror, who receives and distributes spoils. The Psalmist uses "receiving" as evincing the success, Paul "gave" as the act, of the conqueror, who, having subdued his enemies, proceeds to reward his friends. The special application of the passage by Paul was in proof of Christ's exaltation. What the Old Testament represents of His descending and ascending corresponds with His history. He who descended is the same who has ascended. As then ascension was an element of His triumph, so is it now; and He, who, in His humiliation, must be recognized as our vicarious sacrifice and the High Priest of our profession, must also be adored as Head of His Church and author of all her spiritual benefits.

Psalms 72:5.content: as long as … endure—literally, "with the sun," coeval with its existence, and before, or, in presence of the moon, while it lasts (compare Ge 11:28, "before Terah," literally, "in presence of," while he lived).

Psalms 72:6.title: Psalms 72:6
Psalms 72:6.content: A beautiful figure expresses the grateful nature of His influence; 7, and, carrying out the figure, the results are described in an abundant production. the righteous—literally, "righteousness." flourish—literally, "sprout," or, "spring forth."

Psalms 72:8.title: Psalms 72:8
Psalms 72:8.content: The foreign nations mentioned (Ps 72:9, 10) could not be included in the limits, if designed to indicate the boundaries of Solomon's kingdom. The terms, though derived from those used (Ex 23:31; De 11:24) to denote the possessions of Israel, must have a wider sense. Thus, "ends of the earth" is never used of Palestine, but always of the world (compare Margin).

Psalms 72:9.title: Psalms 72:9-11
Psalms 72:9.content: The extent of the conquests. They that dwell in the wilderness—the wild, untutored tribes of deserts. bow … dust—in profound submission. The remotest and wealthiest nations shall acknowledge Him (compare Ps 45:12).

Psalms 72:10.title: Psalms 72:9-11
Psalms 72:10.content: The extent of the conquests. They that dwell in the wilderness—the wild, untutored tribes of deserts. bow … dust—in profound submission. The remotest and wealthiest nations shall acknowledge Him (compare Ps 45:12).

Psalms 72:11.title: Psalms 72:9-11
Psalms 72:11.content: The extent of the conquests. They that dwell in the wilderness—the wild, untutored tribes of deserts. bow … dust—in profound submission. The remotest and wealthiest nations shall acknowledge Him (compare Ps 45:12).

Psalms 72:12.title: Psalms 72:12-14
Psalms 72:12.content: They are not the conquests of arms, but the influences of humane and peaceful principles (compare Isa 9:7; 11:1-9; Zec 9:9, 10).

Psalms 72:13.title: Psalms 72:12-14
Psalms 72:13.content: They are not the conquests of arms, but the influences of humane and peaceful principles (compare Isa 9:7; 11:1-9; Zec 9:9, 10).

Psalms 72:14.title: Psalms 72:12-14
Psalms 72:14.content: They are not the conquests of arms, but the influences of humane and peaceful principles (compare Isa 9:7; 11:1-9; Zec 9:9, 10).

Psalms 72:15.title: Psalms 72:15
Psalms 72:15.content: In his prolonged life he will continue to receive the honorable gifts of the rich, and the prayers of his people shall be made for him, and their praises given to him.

Psalms 72:16.title: Psalms 72:16
Psalms 72:16.content: The spiritual blessings, as often in Scripture, are set forth by material, the abundance of which is described by a figure, in which a "handful" (or literally, "a piece," or small portion) of corn in the most unpropitious locality, shall produce a crop, waving in the wind in its luxuriant growth, like the forests of Lebanon. they of the city … earth—This clause denotes the rapid and abundant increase of population— of—or, "from" the city—Jerusalem, the center and seat of the typical kingdom. flourish—or, glitter as new grass—that is, bloom. This increase corresponds with the increased productiveness. So, as the gospel blessings are diffused, there shall arise increasing recipients of them, out of the Church in which Christ resides as head.

Psalms 72:17.title: Psalms 72:17
Psalms 72:17.content: His name—or, "glorious perfections." as long as the sun—(Compare Ps 72:5). men shall be blessed—(Ge 12:3; 18:18).

Psalms 72:18.title: Psalms 72:18-19
Psalms 72:18.content: These words close the Psalm in terms consistent with the style of the context, while Ps 72:20 is evidently, from its prosaic style, an addition for the purpose above explained [see on Ps 72:1].

Psalms 72:19.title: Psalms 72:18-19
Psalms 72:19.content: These words close the Psalm in terms consistent with the style of the context, while Ps 72:20 is evidently, from its prosaic style, an addition for the purpose above explained [see on Ps 72:1].

Psalms 72:20.title: Psalms 72:20
Psalms 72:20.content: ended—literally, "finished," or completed; the word never denotes fulfilment, except in a very late usage, as in Ezr 1:1; Da 12:7.

Psalms 73:1.title: Psalms 73:1
Psalms 73:1.content: The abrupt announcement of the theme indicates that it is the conclusion of a perplexing mental conflict, which is then detailed (compare Jer 12:1-4). Truly—or, "Surely it is so." clean heart—(Ps 18:26) describes the true Israel.

Psalms 73:2.title: Psalms 73:2
Psalms 73:2.content: The figures express his wavering faith, by terms denoting tottering and weakness (compare Ps 22:5; 62:3).

Psalms 73:3.title: Psalms 73:3-9
Psalms 73:3.content: The prosperous wicked are insolently proud (compare Ps 5:5). They die, as well as live, free from perplexities: pride adorns them, and violence is their clothing; indeed they are inflated with unexpected success. With all this—

Psalms 73:4.title: Psalms 73:3-9
Psalms 73:4.content: The prosperous wicked are insolently proud (compare Ps 5:5). They die, as well as live, free from perplexities: pride adorns them, and violence is their clothing; indeed they are inflated with unexpected success. With all this—

Psalms 73:5.content: The prosperous wicked are insolently proud (compare Ps 5:5). They die, as well as live, free from perplexities: pride adorns them, and violence is their clothing; indeed they are inflated with unexpected success. With all this—
