Psalms 132:17.title: Psalms 132:14-18
Psalms 132:17.content: That choice is expressed in God's words, "I will sit" or "dwell," or sit enthroned. The joy of the people springs from the blessings of His grace, conferred through the medium of the priesthood.

Psalms 132:17.title: Psalms 132:17
Psalms 132:17.content: make the horn … to bud—enlarge his power. a lamp—the figure of prosperity (Ps 18:10, 28; 89:17). With the confounding of his enemies is united his prosperity and the unceasing splendor of his crown.

Psalms 132:18.title: Psalms 132:14-18
Psalms 132:18.content: That choice is expressed in God's words, "I will sit" or "dwell," or sit enthroned. The joy of the people springs from the blessings of His grace, conferred through the medium of the priesthood.

Psalms 133:1.title: Psalms 133:1-2
Psalms 133:1.content: As the fragrant oil is refreshing, so this affords delight. The holy anointing oil for the high priest was olive oil mixed with four of the best spices (Ex 30:22, 25, 30). Its rich profusion typified the abundance of the Spirit's graces. As the copious dew, such as fell on Hermon, falls in fertilizing power on the mountains of Zion, so this unity is fruitful in good works.

Psalms 133:2.title: Psalms 133:1-2
Psalms 133:2.content: As the fragrant oil is refreshing, so this affords delight. The holy anointing oil for the high priest was olive oil mixed with four of the best spices (Ex 30:22, 25, 30). Its rich profusion typified the abundance of the Spirit's graces. As the copious dew, such as fell on Hermon, falls in fertilizing power on the mountains of Zion, so this unity is fruitful in good works.

Psalms 133:3.title: Psalms 133:3
Psalms 133:3.content: there—that is, in Zion, the Church; the material Zion, blessed with enriching dews, suggests this allusion the source of the influence enjoyed by the spiritual Zion. commanded the blessing—(Compare Ps 68:28).

Psalms 134:3.title: Psalms 134:3
Psalms 134:3.content: After the manner directed (Nu 6:23). out of Zion—the Church, as His residence, and thus seat of blessings. Thus close the songs of degrees.

Psalms 135:1.title: Psalms 135:1-3
Psalms 135:1.content: In the general call for praise, the priests, that stand in the house of the Lord, are specially mentioned.

Psalms 135:2.title: Psalms 135:1-3
Psalms 135:2.content: In the general call for praise, the priests, that stand in the house of the Lord, are specially mentioned.

Psalms 135:3.title: Psalms 135:1-3
Psalms 135:3.content: In the general call for praise, the priests, that stand in the house of the Lord, are specially mentioned.

Psalms 135:4.title: Psalms 135:4-7
Psalms 135:4.content: God's choice of Israel is the first reason assigned for rendering praise; the next, His manifested greatness in creation and providence.

Psalms 135:5.title: Psalms 135:4-7
Psalms 135:5.content: God's choice of Israel is the first reason assigned for rendering praise; the next, His manifested greatness in creation and providence.

Psalms 135:6.title: Psalms 135:4-7
Psalms 135:6.content: God's choice of Israel is the first reason assigned for rendering praise; the next, His manifested greatness in creation and providence.

Psalms 135:6.title: Psalms 135:6
Psalms 135:6.content: heaven, and … seas, and all … ends of the earth—denote universality.

Psalms 135:7.title: Psalms 135:4-7
Psalms 135:7.content: God's choice of Israel is the first reason assigned for rendering praise; the next, His manifested greatness in creation and providence.

Psalms 135:8.title: Psalms 135:8-9
Psalms 135:8.content: The last plague [Ex 12:29] is cited to illustrate His "tokens and wonders."

Psalms 135:9.title: Psalms 135:8-9
Psalms 135:9.content: The last plague [Ex 12:29] is cited to illustrate His "tokens and wonders."

Psalms 135:10.title: Psalms 135:10-12
Psalms 135:10.content: The conquest of Canaan was by God's power, not that of the people.

Psalms 135:11.title: Psalms 135:10-12
Psalms 135:11.content: The conquest of Canaan was by God's power, not that of the people.

Psalms 135:12.title: Psalms 135:10-12
Psalms 135:12.content: The conquest of Canaan was by God's power, not that of the people.

Psalms 135:13.title: Psalms 135:13
Psalms 135:13.content: heritage—or, "possession." name … memorial—Each denote that by which God is made known.

Psalms 135:14.title: Psalms 135:14
Psalms 135:14.content: will judge—do justice (Ps 72:2). repent himself—change His dealings (Ps 90:13).

Psalms 135:18.title: Psalms 135:18
Psalms 135:18.content: are like unto them—or, "shall be like," &c. Idolaters become spiritually stupid and perish with their idols (Isa 1:31).

Psalms 135:19.title: Psalms 135:19-21
Psalms 135:19.content: (Compare Ps 115:9-11). There we have "trust" for "bless" here.

Psalms 135:20.title: Psalms 135:19-21
Psalms 135:20.content: (Compare Ps 115:9-11). There we have "trust" for "bless" here.

Psalms 135:21.title: Psalms 135:19-21
Psalms 135:21.content: (Compare Ps 115:9-11). There we have "trust" for "bless" here.

Psalms 135:21.title: Psalms 135:21
Psalms 135:21.content: out of Zion—(Compare Ps 110:2; 134:3). From the Church, as a center, His praise is diffused throughout the earth.

Psalms 136:5.title: Psalms 136:5-6
Psalms 136:5.content: by wisdom—or, "in wisdom" (Ps 104:24). made—literally, "maker of." above the waters—or, "higher than the waters" (Ps 24:2).

Psalms 136:6.title: Psalms 136:5-6
Psalms 136:6.content: by wisdom—or, "in wisdom" (Ps 104:24). made—literally, "maker of." above the waters—or, "higher than the waters" (Ps 24:2).

Psalms 136:15.title: Psalms 136:15
Psalms 136:15.content: overthrew—literally, "shook off," as in Ex 14:27, as a contemptuous rejection of a reptile.

Psalms 136:23.title: Psalms 136:23
Psalms 136:23.content: remembered us—or, "for us" (Ps 132:1). our low estate—that is, captivity.

Psalms 136:24.title: Psalms 136:24
Psalms 136:24.content: And hath redeemed us—or, literally, "snatched us"—alluding to the sudden deliverance effected by the overthrow of Babylon.

Psalms 136:25.title: Psalms 136:25
Psalms 136:25.content: To the special favors to His people is added the record of God's goodness to all His creatures (compare Mt 6:30).

Psalms 136:26.title: Psalms 136:26
Psalms 136:26.content: God of heaven—occurs but once (Jon 1:9) before the captivity. It is used by the later writers as specially distinguishing God from idols.

Psalms 137:1.title: Psalms 137:1
Psalms 137:1.content: rivers of Babylon—the name of the city used for the whole country. remembered Zion—or, Jerusalem, as in Ps 132:13.

Psalms 137:2.title: Psalms 137:2
Psalms 137:2.content: upon the willows—which may have grown there then, if not now; as the palm, which was once common, is now rare in Palestine.

Psalms 137:3.title: Psalms 137:3-4
Psalms 137:3.content: Whether the request was in curiosity or derision, the answer intimates that a compliance was incongruous with their mournful feelings (Pr 25:20).

Psalms 137:4.title: Psalms 137:3-4
Psalms 137:4.content: Whether the request was in curiosity or derision, the answer intimates that a compliance was incongruous with their mournful feelings (Pr 25:20).

Psalms 137:5.title: Psalms 137:5-6
Psalms 137:5.content: For joyful songs would imply forgetfulness of their desolated homes and fallen Church. The solemn imprecations on the hand and tongue, if thus forgetful, relate to the cunning or skill in playing, and the power of singing.

Psalms 137:6.title: Psalms 137:5-6
Psalms 137:6.content: For joyful songs would imply forgetfulness of their desolated homes and fallen Church. The solemn imprecations on the hand and tongue, if thus forgetful, relate to the cunning or skill in playing, and the power of singing.

Psalms 137:7.title: Psalms 137:7-9
Psalms 137:7.content: Remember … the children of Edom—(Compare Ps 132:1), that is, to punish. the day of Jerusalem—its downfall (La 4:21, 22; Ob 11-13).

Psalms 137:8.title: Psalms 137:7-9
Psalms 137:8.content: Remember … the children of Edom—(Compare Ps 132:1), that is, to punish. the day of Jerusalem—its downfall (La 4:21, 22; Ob 11-13).

Psalms 137:8.title: Psalms 137:8
Psalms 137:8.content: daughter of Babylon—the people (Ps 9:13). Their destruction had been abundantly foretold (Isa 13:14; Jer 51:23). For the terribleness of that destruction, God's righteous judgment, and not the passions of the chafed Israelites, was responsible.

Psalms 137:9.title: Psalms 137:7-9
Psalms 137:9.content: Remember … the children of Edom—(Compare Ps 132:1), that is, to punish. the day of Jerusalem—its downfall (La 4:21, 22; Ob 11-13).

Psalms 138:1.title: Psalms 138:1
Psalms 138:1.content: I will praise thee with my whole heart—(Compare Ps 9:1). before the gods—whether angels (Ps 8:5); or princes (Ex 21:6; Ps 82:6); or idols (Ps 97:7); denotes a readiness to worship the true God alone, and a contempt of all other objects of worship.

Psalms 138:2.title: Psalms 138:2
Psalms 138:2.content: (Compare Ps 5:7). thy word above all thy name—that is, God's promise (2Sa 7:12-16), sustained by His mercy and truth, exceeded all other manifestations of Himself as subject of praise.

Psalms 138:3.title: Psalms 138:3-5
Psalms 138:3.content: That promise, as an answer to his prayers in distress, revived and strengthened his faith; and, as the basis of other revelations of the Messiah, it will be the occasion of praise by all who hear and receive it (Ps 68:29, 31; Isa 4:3).

Psalms 138:4.title: Psalms 138:3-5
Psalms 138:4.content: That promise, as an answer to his prayers in distress, revived and strengthened his faith; and, as the basis of other revelations of the Messiah, it will be the occasion of praise by all who hear and receive it (Ps 68:29, 31; Isa 4:3).

Psalms 138:5.title: Psalms 138:3-5
Psalms 138:5.content: That promise, as an answer to his prayers in distress, revived and strengthened his faith; and, as the basis of other revelations of the Messiah, it will be the occasion of praise by all who hear and receive it (Ps 68:29, 31; Isa 4:3).

Psalms 138:5.title: Psalms 138:5
Psalms 138:5.content: for great is the glory—or, "when the glory shall be great," in God's fulfilling His purposes of redemption.

Psalms 138:6.title: Psalms 138:6-7
Psalms 138:6.content: On this general principle of God's government (Isa 2:11; 57:15; 66:2), he relies for God's favor in saving him, and overthrowing his enemies. knoweth afar off—their ways and deserts (Ps 1:6).

Psalms 138:7.title: Psalms 138:6-7
Psalms 138:7.content: On this general principle of God's government (Isa 2:11; 57:15; 66:2), he relies for God's favor in saving him, and overthrowing his enemies. knoweth afar off—their ways and deserts (Ps 1:6).

Psalms 140:1.title: Psalms 140:1
Psalms 140:1.content: evil man—Which of David's enemies is meant is not important.

Psalms 140:2.title: Psalms 140:2-5
Psalms 140:2.content: This character of the wicked, and the devices planned against the pious, correspond to Ps 10:7; 31:13; 58:4, &c.

Psalms 140:3.title: Psalms 140:2-5
Psalms 140:3.content: This character of the wicked, and the devices planned against the pious, correspond to Ps 10:7; 31:13; 58:4, &c.

Psalms 140:3.title: Psalms 140:3
Psalms 140:3.content: sharpened … like a serpent—not like a serpent does, but they are thus like a serpent in cunning and venom.

Psalms 140:4.title: Psalms 140:2-5
Psalms 140:4.content: This character of the wicked, and the devices planned against the pious, correspond to Ps 10:7; 31:13; 58:4, &c.

Psalms 140:5.title: Psalms 140:2-5
Psalms 140:5.content: This character of the wicked, and the devices planned against the pious, correspond to Ps 10:7; 31:13; 58:4, &c.

Psalms 140:7.title: Psalms 140:7
Psalms 140:7.content: day of battle—literally, "of armor," that is, when using it.

Psalms 140:8.title: Psalms 140:8
Psalms 140:8.content: (Compare Ps 37:12; 66:7). lest they exalt themselves—or, they will be exalted if permitted to prosper.

Psalms 140:9.title: Psalms 140:9
Psalms 140:9.content: Contrasts his head covered by God (Ps 140:7) with theirs, or (as "head" may be used for "persons") with them, covered with the results of their wicked deeds (Ps 7:16).

Psalms 140:10.title: Psalms 140:10
Psalms 140:10.content: (Compare Ps 11:6; 120:4). cast into the fire; into deep pits—figures for utter destruction.

Psalms 140:11.title: Psalms 140:11
Psalms 140:11.content: an evil speaker—or, "slanderer" will not be tolerated (Ps 101:7). The last clause may be translated: "an evil (man) He (God) shall hunt," &c.

Psalms 140:13.title: Psalms 140:13
Psalms 140:13.content: After all changes, the righteous shall have cause for praise. Such shall dwell—shall sit securely, under God's protection (Ps 21:6; 41:12).

Psalms 142:2.title: Psalms 142:2
Psalms 142:2.content: (Compare Ps 62:8). I poured out my complaint—or, "a sad musing."

Psalms 142:3.title: Psalms 142:3
Psalms 142:3.content: thou knewest … path—The appeal is indicative of conscious innocence; knowest it to be right, and that my affliction is owing to the snares of enemies, and is not deserved (compare Ps 42:4; 61:2).

Psalms 142:4.title: Psalms 142:4
Psalms 142:4.content: Utter desolation is meant. right hand—the place of a protector (Ps 110:5). cared for—literally, "sought after," to do good.

Psalms 142:7.title: Psalms 142:7
Psalms 142:7.content: (Compare Ps 25:17). that I may praise—literally, "for praising," or, "that Thy name may be praised," that is, by the righteous, who shall surround me with sympathizing joy (Ps 35:27).

Psalms 143:1.title: Psalms 143:1
Psalms 143:1.content: in thy faithfulness … and … righteousness—or, God's regard to the claims which He has permitted His people to make in His covenant.

Psalms 143:2.title: Psalms 143:2
Psalms 143:2.content: enter … judgment—deal not in strict justice. shall no … justified—or, "is no man justified," or "innocent" (Job 14:3; Ro 3:20).

Psalms 143:3.title: Psalms 143:3-4
Psalms 143:3.content: The exciting reason for his prayer—his afflictions—led to confession as just made: he now makes the complaint. as those that have been long dead—deprived of life's comforts (compare Ps 40:15; 88:3-6).

Psalms 143:4.title: Psalms 143:3-4
Psalms 143:4.content: The exciting reason for his prayer—his afflictions—led to confession as just made: he now makes the complaint. as those that have been long dead—deprived of life's comforts (compare Ps 40:15; 88:3-6).

Psalms 143:5.title: Psalms 143:5-6
Psalms 143:5.content: The distress is aggravated by the contrast of former comfort (Ps 22:3-5), for whose return he longs. a thirsty land—which needs rain, as did his spirit God's gracious visits (Ps 28:1; 89:17).

Psalms 143:6.title: Psalms 143:5-6
Psalms 143:6.content: The distress is aggravated by the contrast of former comfort (Ps 22:3-5), for whose return he longs. a thirsty land—which needs rain, as did his spirit God's gracious visits (Ps 28:1; 89:17).

Psalms 143:8.title: Psalms 143:8
Psalms 143:8.content: (Compare Ps 25:1-4; 59:16). the way … walk—that is, the way of safety and righteousness (Ps 142:3-6).

Psalms 143:10.title: Psalms 143:10
Psalms 143:10.content: (Compare Ps 5:8; 27:11). land of uprightness—literally, "an even land" (Ps 26:12).

Psalms 143:12.title: Psalms 143:12
Psalms 143:12.content: God's mercy to His people is often wrath to His and their enemies (compare Ps 31:17). thy servant—as chosen to be such, entitled to divine regard.

Psalms 145:1.title: Psalms 145:1-2
Psalms 145:1.content: (Compare Ps 30:1). bless thy name—celebrate Thy perfections (Ps 5:11). God is addressed as king, alluding to His government of men.

Psalms 145:2.title: Psalms 145:1-2
Psalms 145:2.content: (Compare Ps 30:1). bless thy name—celebrate Thy perfections (Ps 5:11). God is addressed as king, alluding to His government of men.

Psalms 145:3.title: Psalms 145:3
Psalms 145:3.content: (Compare Ps 18:3; 48:1). greatness—as displayed in His works.

Psalms 145:4.title: Psalms 145:4
Psalms 145:4.content: shall declare—literally, "they shall declare," that is, all generations.

Psalms 145:5.title: Psalms 145:5
Psalms 145:5.content: I will speak—or, "muse" (Ps 77:12; 119:15). thy wondrous works—or, "words of thy wonders," that is, which described them (Ps 105:27, Margin).

Psalms 145:6.title: Psalms 145:6
Psalms 145:6.content: terrible acts—which produce dread or fear.

Psalms 145:7.title: Psalms 145:7
Psalms 145:7.content: memory—(Ps 6:5), remembrance, or what causes to be remembered. righteousness—as in Ps 143:1, goodness according to covenant engagement.

Psalms 145:8.title: Psalms 145:8-9
Psalms 145:8.content: (Compare Ps 103:8; 111:4). over all, &c.—rests on all His works.

Psalms 145:9.title: Psalms 145:8-9
Psalms 145:9.content: (Compare Ps 103:8; 111:4). over all, &c.—rests on all His works.

Psalms 145:10.title: Psalms 145:10
Psalms 145:10.content: bless—as in Ps 145:1, to praise with reverence, more than merely to praise.

Psalms 145:11.title: Psalms 145:11-12
Psalms 145:11.content: The declaration of God's glory is for the extension of His knowledge and perfections in the world.

Psalms 145:12.title: Psalms 145:11-12
Psalms 145:12.content: The declaration of God's glory is for the extension of His knowledge and perfections in the world.

Psalms 145:15.title: Psalms 145:15-16
Psalms 145:15.content: eyes of … thee—or, look with expecting faith (Ps 104:27, 28).

Psalms 145:16.title: Psalms 145:15-16
Psalms 145:16.content: eyes of … thee—or, look with expecting faith (Ps 104:27, 28).

Psalms 145:17.title: Psalms 145:17
Psalms 145:17.content: holy … works—literally, "merciful" or "kind, goodness" (Ps 144:2) is the corresponding noun. righteous—in a similar relation of meaning to "righteousness" (Ps 145:7).

Psalms 145:20.title: Psalms 145:20
Psalms 145:20.content: Those who fear Him (Ps 145:19) are those who are here said to love Him.

Psalms 145:21.title: Psalms 145:21
Psalms 145:21.content: (Compare Ps 33:21). all flesh—(Ps 65:2). The Psalm ends, as it began, with ascriptions of praise, in which the pious will ever delight to join.

Psalms 147:3.title: Psalms 147:3
Psalms 147:3.content: Though applicable to the captive Israelites, this is a general and precious truth. wounds—(Compare Margin).

Psalms 147:4.title: Psalms 147:4-5
Psalms 147:4.content: God's power in nature (Isa 40:26-28, and often) is presented as a pledge of His power to help His people. telleth … stars—what no man can do (Ge 15:5).

Psalms 147:5.title: Psalms 147:4-5
Psalms 147:5.content: God's power in nature (Isa 40:26-28, and often) is presented as a pledge of His power to help His people. telleth … stars—what no man can do (Ge 15:5).

Psalms 147:6.title: Psalms 147:6
Psalms 147:6.content: That power is put forth for the good of the meek and suffering pious, and confusion of the wicked (Ps 146:8, 9).

Psalms 147:7.title: Psalms 147:7-9
Psalms 147:7.content: His providence supplies bountifully the wild animals in their mountain homes. Sing … Lord—literally, "Answer the Lord," that is, in grateful praise to His goodness, thus declared in His acts.

Psalms 147:8.title: Psalms 147:7-9
Psalms 147:8.content: His providence supplies bountifully the wild animals in their mountain homes. Sing … Lord—literally, "Answer the Lord," that is, in grateful praise to His goodness, thus declared in His acts.

Psalms 147:9.title: Psalms 147:7-9
Psalms 147:9.content: His providence supplies bountifully the wild animals in their mountain homes. Sing … Lord—literally, "Answer the Lord," that is, in grateful praise to His goodness, thus declared in His acts.

Psalms 147:10.title: Psalms 147:10-11
Psalms 147:10.content: The advantages afforded, as in war by the strength of the horse or the agility of man, do not incline God to favor any; but those who fear and, of course, trust Him, will obtain His approbation and aid.

Psalms 147:11.title: Psalms 147:10-11
Psalms 147:11.content: The advantages afforded, as in war by the strength of the horse or the agility of man, do not incline God to favor any; but those who fear and, of course, trust Him, will obtain His approbation and aid.

Psalms 147:13.title: Psalms 147:13
Psalms 147:13.content: strengthened … gates—or, means of defense against invaders,

Psalms 147:14.title: Psalms 147:14
Psalms 147:14.content: maketh … borders—or, territories (Ge 23:17; Isa 54:12). filleth thee, &c.—(Compare Margin).

Psalms 147:15.title: Psalms 147:15-18
Psalms 147:15.content: God's Word, as a swift messenger, executes His purpose, for with Him to command is to perform (Ge 1:3; Ps 33:9), and He brings about the wonders of providence as easily as men cast crumbs.

Psalms 147:16.title: Psalms 147:15-18
Psalms 147:16.content: God's Word, as a swift messenger, executes His purpose, for with Him to command is to perform (Ge 1:3; Ps 33:9), and He brings about the wonders of providence as easily as men cast crumbs.

Psalms 147:17.title: Psalms 147:15-18
Psalms 147:17.content: God's Word, as a swift messenger, executes His purpose, for with Him to command is to perform (Ge 1:3; Ps 33:9), and He brings about the wonders of providence as easily as men cast crumbs.

Psalms 147:17.title: Psalms 147:17
Psalms 147:17.content: morsels—used as to food (Ge 18:5), perhaps here denotes hail.

Psalms 147:18.title: Psalms 147:15-18
Psalms 147:18.content: God's Word, as a swift messenger, executes His purpose, for with Him to command is to perform (Ge 1:3; Ps 33:9), and He brings about the wonders of providence as easily as men cast crumbs.

Psalms 147:19.title: Psalms 147:19-20
Psalms 147:19.content: This mighty ruler and benefactor of heaven and earth is such especially to His chosen people, to whom alone (De 4:32-34) He has made known His will, while others have been left in darkness. Therefore unite in the great hallelujah.

Psalms 147:20.title: Psalms 147:19-20
Psalms 147:20.content: This mighty ruler and benefactor of heaven and earth is such especially to His chosen people, to whom alone (De 4:32-34) He has made known His will, while others have been left in darkness. Therefore unite in the great hallelujah.

Psalms 148:4.title: Psalms 148:4
Psalms 148:4.content: heavens of heavens—the very highest. waters—clouds, resting above the visible heavens (compare Ge 1:7).

Psalms 148:5.title: Psalms 148:5
Psalms 148:5.content: praise the name—as representing His perfections. he commanded—"He" is emphatic, ascribing creation to God alone.

Psalms 148:6.title: Psalms 148:6
Psalms 148:6.content: The perpetuity of the frame of nature is, of course, subject to Him who formed it. a decree … pass—His ordinances respecting them shall not change (Jer 36:31), or perish (Job 34:20; Ps 37:36).

Psalms 148:7.title: Psalms 148:7-10
Psalms 148:7.content: The call on the earth, as opposed to heaven, includes seas or depths, whose inhabitants the dragon, as one of the largest (on leviathan, see on Ps 104:26), is selected to represent. The most destructive and ungovernable agents of inanimate nature are introduced.

Psalms 148:8.title: Psalms 148:7-10
Psalms 148:8.content: The call on the earth, as opposed to heaven, includes seas or depths, whose inhabitants the dragon, as one of the largest (on leviathan, see on Ps 104:26), is selected to represent. The most destructive and ungovernable agents of inanimate nature are introduced.

Psalms 148:8.title: Psalms 148:8
Psalms 148:8.content: fulfilling his word—or, law, may be understood of each. Next the most distinguished productions of the vegetable world.

Psalms 148:9.title: Psalms 148:7-10
Psalms 148:9.content: The call on the earth, as opposed to heaven, includes seas or depths, whose inhabitants the dragon, as one of the largest (on leviathan, see on Ps 104:26), is selected to represent. The most destructive and ungovernable agents of inanimate nature are introduced.

Psalms 148:9.title: Psalms 148:9
Psalms 148:9.content: fruitful trees—or, "trees of fruit," as opposed to forest trees. Wild and domestic, large and small animals are comprehended.

Psalms 148:10.title: Psalms 148:7-10
Psalms 148:10.content: The call on the earth, as opposed to heaven, includes seas or depths, whose inhabitants the dragon, as one of the largest (on leviathan, see on Ps 104:26), is selected to represent. The most destructive and ungovernable agents of inanimate nature are introduced.

Psalms 148:11.title: Psalms 148:11-12
Psalms 148:11.content: Next all rational beings, from the highest in rank to little children. princes—or, military leaders.

Psalms 148:12.title: Psalms 148:11-12
Psalms 148:12.content: Next all rational beings, from the highest in rank to little children. princes—or, military leaders.

Psalms 148:13.title: Psalms 148:13
Psalms 148:13.content: Let them—all mentioned. excellent—or, exalted (Isa 12:4). his glory—majesty (Ps 45:3). above the earth and heaven—Their united splendors fail to match His.

Psalms 148:14.title: Psalms 148:14
Psalms 148:14.content: exalteth the horn—established power (Ps 75:5, 6). praise of—or literally, "for" his saints—that is, occasions for them to praise Him. They are further described as "His people," and "near unto Him," sustaining by covenanted care a peculiarly intimate relation.

Psalms 149:2.title: Psalms 149:2
Psalms 149:2.content: God had signalized His relation as a sovereign, in restoring them to their land.

Psalms 149:3.title: Psalms 149:3
Psalms 149:3.content: in the dance—(Ps 30:11). The dance is connected with other terms, expressive of the great joy of the occasion. The word may be rendered "lute," to which the other instruments are joined. sing praises—or, sing and play.

Psalms 149:4.title: Psalms 149:4
Psalms 149:4.content: taketh pleasure—literally, "accepts," alluding to acceptance of propitiatory offerings (compare Ps 147:11). beautify, &c.—adorn the humble with faith, hope, joy, and peace.

Psalms 149:5.title: Psalms 149:5
Psalms 149:5.content: in glory—the honorable condition to which they are raised. upon their beds—once a place of mourning (Ps 6:6).

Psalms 149:6.title: Psalms 149:6
Psalms 149:6.content: high praises—or, "deeds." They shall go forth as religious warriors, as once religious laborers (Ne 4:17).

Psalms 149:7.title: Psalms 149:7
Psalms 149:7.content: The destruction of the incorrigibly wicked attends the propagation of God's truth, so that the military successes of the Jews, after the captivity, typified the triumphs of the Gospel.

Psalms 149:9.title: Psalms 149:9
Psalms 149:9.content: the judgment written—either in God's decrees, or perhaps as in De 32:41-43. this honour—that is, to be thus employed, will be an honorable service, to be assigned his saints—or, godly ones (Ps 16:3).

Psalms 150:1.title: Psalms 150:1
Psalms 150:1.content: in his sanctuary—on earth. firmament of his power—which illustrates His power.

Psalms 150:2.title: Psalms 150:2
Psalms 150:2.content: mighty acts—(Ps 145:4). excellent greatness—or, abundance of greatness.

Psalms 150:4.title: Psalms 150:4
Psalms 150:4.content: organs—or pipe, a wind instrument, and the others were used in worship.

Psalms 150:6.title: Psalms 150:6
Psalms 150:6.content: LIVING VOICES SHALL TAKE UP THE FAILING SOUNDS OF DEAD INSTRUMENTS, AND AS THEY CEASE ON EARTH,THOSE OF INTELLIGENT RANSOMED SPIRITS AND HOLY ANGELS,AS WITH THE SOUND OF MIGHTY THUNDERS, WILL PROLONG ETERNALLY THE PRAISE, SAYING: "ALLELUIA! SALVATION, AND GLORY, AND HONOR, AND POWER, UNTO THE LORD OUR GOD;" "ALLELUIA! FOR THE LORD GOD OMNIPOTENT REIGNETH." AMEN!
